title: Missing Monitoring Data
prompt: A monitoring agent sends a normal value every minute. If consecutive missing data continues for a sufficient period, the existing CloudWatch alarm should enter the ALARM state after the last normal value falls outside the evaluation range. Which missing-data treatment should be used?

choices.text: Treat missing data as not breaching
choices.explanation: The resource may still be judged healthy even when the monitored target cannot send metrics.

choices.text: Treat missing data as ignore
choices.explanation: If the last state was OK, missing data does not change the alarm to ALARM.

choices.text: Leave the evaluation period unset
choices.explanation: This does not make an evaluation period unnecessary and does not define how missing data is judged.

choices.text: Treat missing data as breaching
choices.explanation: A state in which observations have stopped can be included in the evaluation as a threshold violation.

source.label: CloudWatchアラームの欠損データの扱い

learning.reason: A state in which observations have stopped can be included in the evaluation as a threshold violation.
learning.concept: The meaning of missing data depends on the metric. For metrics emitted only during abnormal conditions, treating missing data as not breaching can also be an appropriate design.

title: Recovering from an Incorrect Update
prompt: At 14:00, multiple tables in the production RDS database were updated incorrectly. Compare the data at 13:59, which is within the backup retention period, with the current data without interrupting normal production processing. The available manual snapshot is from the previous day only.

choices.explanation: The updates are also replicated to the standby, so this does not restore the database to an earlier point in time.

choices.text: Reboot the current DB
choices.explanation: Rebooting does not revert incorrectly updated data.

choices.text: Restore a separate DB from the previous day's manual snapshot
choices.explanation: Production would not be stopped, but the restored data would not be from the required time.

choices.text: Create a separate DB by using point-in-time restore
choices.explanation: You can restore a new DB to a specified time within the backup retention period.

learning.reason: You can restore a new DB to a specified time within the backup retention period.

title: Monitoring Without Detaching Under High Load
prompt: The EC2 instances behind an ALB temporarily slow down under high load because they are waiting for database connections. The current health check runs a heavy database query, causing all instances to be marked unhealthy at the same time. You want to detect failed applications while notifying the operations team separately about failures in the shared database.

choices.text: Configure a lightweight process check on the ALB and monitor the database with a separate alarm
choices.explanation: This separates the decision to detach an instance from operational notification about a shared dependency.

choices.text: Only increase the health check timeout
choices.explanation: This may help with temporary delays, but it does not distinguish database failures from application failures.

choices.text: Change the ALB health check to an even heavier business transaction
choices.explanation: This worsens the problem of all instances becoming unhealthy when the shared dependency fails.

choices.text: Treat every HTTP status as successful
choices.explanation: This would also treat responses from failed applications as healthy.

source.label: Amazon Builders’ Libraryのヘルスチェック

learning.reason: This separates the decision to detach an instance from operational notification about a shared dependency.
learning.concept: Use different monitoring mechanisms for the decision to remove an instance from load balancing and for notifying operators about dependency failures.

title: Monitoring that does not treat intermittent latency as consecutive breaches
prompt: An API's p95 is evaluated every 5 minutes. An alarm should be triggered when any 2 periods in the most recent 20 minutes exceed the threshold; the breaches do not need to be consecutive. Metrics are reported for all 4 periods. Which configuration meets the requirements?

choices.text: Set EvaluationPeriods to 4 and DatapointsToAlarm to 4.
choices.explanation: The alarm will trigger only if every period being evaluated exceeds the threshold.

choices.text: Set EvaluationPeriods to 2 and DatapointsToAlarm to 2.
choices.explanation: This triggers only when both of the most recent 2 periods exceed the threshold, so it cannot detect 2 nonconsecutive breaches within 20 minutes.

choices.text: Set EvaluationPeriods to 4 and DatapointsToAlarm to 2.
choices.explanation: The requirement is met when 2 of the 4 periods being evaluated exceed the threshold, even if the breaches are not consecutive.

choices.text: Set Period to 20 minutes and EvaluationPeriods to 1 while keeping only the p95 threshold.
choices.explanation: Because the entire 20 minutes is evaluated as one statistic, the number of breaches in 5-minute periods cannot be determined.

source.label: CloudWatchのM out of Nアラーム

learning.reason: EvaluationPeriods is the number of periods examined, while DatapointsToAlarm is the required number of breaches among those periods.
learning.concept: For intermittent failures, evaluating one statistic over a longer period behaves differently from counting threshold breaches across multiple shorter periods.

title: Exclude unused detailed dimensions from transmission
prompt: Use Amazon CloudWatch Agent to collect some disk metrics from all EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. You added AutoScalingGroupName to aggregation_dimensions, enabling group-level monitoring, but the original per-instance time series are also being sent, increasing costs. How can you limit only the target metrics to group aggregation while retaining per-instance information for other metrics?

choices.text: Remove AutoScalingGroupName from append_dimensions for all metrics.
choices.explanation: This would also remove the group dimension needed for aggregation and would not change only the target metrics.

choices.text: Remove aggregation_dimensions and aggregate all per-instance time series in the console.
choices.explanation: The original time series would still be sent, so the cost of unnecessary time series would not be reduced.

choices.text: Change only metrics_collection_interval to 24 hours.
choices.explanation: This changes the sampling frequency, but the original per-instance metrics remain and daytime monitoring accuracy also changes.

choices.text: List the target disk metrics in drop_original_metrics while retaining aggregation by AutoScalingGroupName.
choices.explanation: Only the specified original per-instance time series are no longer sent, while the aggregated time series remain.

source.label: CloudWatch Agentの設定ファイル

learning.reason: Adding an aggregation dimension alone does not stop metrics with their original dimensions from being transmitted.
learning.concept: To omit per-instance metrics, retain the dimension needed for aggregation and specify, metric by metric, that transmission of the original series should stop.

title: Separate recovery behavior for host failures and guest OS failures
prompt: A business service runs on an EC2 instance, and downtime should be avoided. If an underlying hardware failure is detected, the EC2 recovery action should attempt to move the instance to another host. The same recovery must not be triggered by an application-caused guest startup failure. The instance supports recovery actions through CloudWatch actions. On which metric should the recovery action be configured?

choices.text: Add the EC2 recovery action to an alarm for StatusCheckFailed_System.
choices.explanation: Only a system status check failure on the underlying infrastructure can be used as the recovery condition.

choices.text: Monitor only the total StatusCheckFailed value and use the same action for any failed check.
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish failures on the underlying infrastructure from failures inside the instance.

choices.text: Recover the instance when CPUUtilization is low.
choices.explanation: CPU utilization can be low even when the instance is idle, so it cannot identify an underlying infrastructure failure.

choices.text: Configure the recovery action for StatusCheckFailed_Instance and treat an application startup error as an infrastructure failure.
choices.explanation: The instance status check includes problems on the guest side and is not limited to infrastructure failures.

source.label: EC2ステータスチェックのアラーム

learning.reason: A system status check concerns the host and underlying infrastructure.
learning.concept: Use different health signals for recovery actions inside the guest and EC2 recovery that replaces the underlying host.

title: I/O saturation when all EBS volumes have sufficient capacity
prompt: Use multiple gp3 volumes with a corresponding Nitro-based EC2 instance. I/O is delayed during a batch, but VolumeIOPSExceededCheck is 0 for every volume. InstanceEBSIOPSExceededCheck is 1 on the EC2 instance at the same time, and no throughput exceedance is observed. What should be adjusted next?

choices.text: Increase the CloudWatch Agent collection interval to reduce the exceedance metrics.
choices.explanation: Changing the observation frequency does not change the instance's I/O constraint.

choices.text: On the same instance, increase only the provisioned IOPS of all gp3 volumes.
choices.explanation: Increasing the limit of each volume does not change the aggregate IOPS limit on the EC2 instance.

choices.text: Increase only throughput to raise the MiB/s limit.
choices.explanation: The observation indicates an excess of processable I/O operations, not a throughput exceedance.

choices.text: Check the EBS IOPS limit assigned to the instance and, if necessary, change to an instance type with higher EBS IOPS.
choices.explanation: The instance has reached the IOPS it can process across its connections, so increasing the limit of individual volumes will not solve the issue.

source.label: EC2のCloudWatchメトリクス

learning.reason: The per-volume limit and the limit for all EBS volumes attached to an instance are separate.
learning.concept: Before increasing the performance of a specific volume, determine whether the volume-side or EC2-side limit has been exhausted.

title: View time series from multiple accounts in a monitoring account
prompt: Three accounts in the same Region have CloudWatch application metrics. The existing monitoring in each account must remain in place, while operators need to view the metrics from a central monitoring account without switching roles. Which configuration is required? Select two.

choices.text: Create a monitoring sink with the same name in each source account, but do not link it to the central account.
choices.explanation: The source accounts must be connected to the central sink for the central monitoring account to view the metrics.

choices.text: Use the same namespace in each account and create a dashboard with the same name in the central CloudWatch account.
choices.explanation: Matching names do not provide permission or cross-account integration for viewing metrics in another account.

choices.text: Create a sink in the monitoring account and allow attachments from each source account.
choices.explanation: This configures the central monitoring account to accept the shared data.

choices.text: Send all time series names to the same CloudWatch Logs log group.
choices.explanation: Recording metric names in a log group does not make the original time series directly viewable in CloudWatch.

choices.text: Create a link from each source account to the monitoring account's sink and select metric sharing.
choices.explanation: This allows the existing source metrics to be viewed without republishing duplicate metrics.

source.label: CloudWatchのクロスアカウント可観測性

learning.reason: The sink is configured on the monitoring side to accept sharing, while the links configure sharing from the source side.
learning.concept: The Region and data types shared for central viewing can be configured without moving management of the existing metrics to another account.

prompt: You want to continuously send new ERROR entries arriving in the app's CloudWatch Logs to an existing aggregation Lambda. choices.text: Add a subscription filter with an ERROR condition to the target log group and allow invocation of the Lambda.

title: Customer-specific time series proliferate in log aggregation
prompt: The team creates CloudWatch metrics from order logs to monitor error trends by API route. The current metric filter uses the route and a unique requestId as dimensions. choices.text: Remove the route from the dimensions and retain only requestId.
choices.explanation: This leaves a time series for each request and also loses route-level monitoring.

choices.text: Remove requestId from the metric dimensions and aggregate by route only.
choices.explanation: This preserves the required route-level monitoring and limits the number of time series created for unique IDs.

choices.text: Shorten the log group's retention period.
choices.explanation: Deleting logs does not change the high cardinality at metric publication time.

choices.text: Change the unit from Count to None.
choices.explanation: A metric's unit does not reduce the number of dimension combinations.

learning.reason: Each distinct combination of dimension values creates a separate metric time series.

title: Distinguish Requests Rejected by the Concurrency Limit
prompt: A process that invokes a Lambda function synchronously has seen an increase in TooManyRequestsException. The function's reserved concurrency is 40, and ConcurrentExecutions remains at 40 at the same time, while the account concurrency limit has ample headroom. The function's Errors metric has not increased. What should be reviewed?

choices.text: Confirm the amount of processing the downstream systems can accept and, if necessary, increase the function's reserved concurrency.
choices.explanation: Changing the function-specific limit allows a value to be selected that does not overload downstream systems.

choices.text: Only increase the function timeout.
choices.explanation: This does not increase the number of executions that can be accepted, and longer executions can occupy the available concurrency for longer.

choices.text: Only request an increase to the account concurrency quota.
choices.explanation: The explicit limit of 40 on the function would remain unchanged.

choices.text: Shorten the evaluation interval for Errors in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This does not change the available execution capacity when requests are rejected.

source.label: Lambdaの予約済み同時実行数

learning.reason: Reserved concurrency is also the maximum number of concurrent executions for that function.
learning.concept: When an invocation is rejected, the handler does not run, so the rejection is not reflected in the function's error count.

title: Investigate Incomplete Parts Across Many Buckets
prompt: Storage costs have increased across multiple S3 buckets. Without storing routine access logs, you want to use a management dashboard to determine which buckets have many incomplete multipart uploads. What should you use?

choices.explanation: Incomplete parts cannot be aggregated from an inventory of objects.

learning.reason: S3 Storage Lens aggregates the number of incomplete parts and the bytes they use.
