title: Only the Read Replica Is Stale After a Successful Write
prompt: Saving an order to the writer of RDS for MySQL succeeds immediately. Only when an immediate subsequent query is sent to a read replica through a separate connection is the latest order missing. Both instances have sufficient CPU, and CloudWatch ReplicaLag is increasing. How should the application restore the screen immediately after confirmation?

choices.text: When ReplicaLag increases, first extend only the RDS backup retention period.
choices.explanation: Backup retention and the time at which changes reach a read replica are separate concerns.

choices.text: After saving to the writer, recreate the TCP connection to the same replica.
choices.explanation: If the destination is the same, changes that have not yet been applied still cannot be seen.

choices.text: Monitor ReplicaLag and send queries made immediately after confirmation to the writer.
choices.explanation: Requests that require the latest state are no longer dependent on the replica's replication delay.

choices.text: Send all queries to the replica and reduce the writer's CPU utilization.
choices.explanation: This does not change the required consistency and leaves important reads exposed to replication delay.

source.label: RDSのリードレプリカの監視

learning.reason: Read replicas apply changes asynchronously, so recent writes may not be readable from a replica while lag exists.
learning.concept: Route queries that require the state immediately after an update separately from reads that can tolerate replication delay.

categoryLabel: Monitoring, analysis, remediation, and performance optimization
examDomainLabel: Monitoring, analysis, remediation, and performance optimization

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Level Demand According to the Number of Instances
prompt: A web service runs on identical-performance EC2 instances behind an ALB. The number of requests correlates with load, and you want to keep the number of requests processed per healthy target approximately constant. The start and end times of business hours and other scaling times cannot be predicted. Which Auto Scaling configuration should be used?

choices.text: Schedule scaling only at the start and end of business hours.
choices.explanation: This does not follow demand changes that occur at unpredictable times.

choices.text: Fix DesiredCapacity and adjust load only through the target group's health checks.
choices.explanation: Health checks determine reachability; they do not adjust capacity according to demand.

choices.text: Configure target tracking on the ALB-wide RequestCount metric.
choices.explanation: Total demand remains the same even when more instances are added, so it does not signal that per-instance load should return to the target value.

choices.text: Select ALBRequestCountPerTarget and specify the target group and target value.
choices.explanation: This evaluates requests per target and can adjust the number of instances accordingly.

source.label: EC2 Auto Scalingのターゲット追跡

learning.reason: Use a metric whose per-unit load changes when capacity changes as the target for scaling.
learning.concept: Target tracking adjusts capacity to bring the metric back near its target value.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Join the service after retrieving updated endpoint protection settings
prompt: A new Auto Scaling instance retrieves a fixed monitoring ID and configuration from a distribution server after launch. Processing time varies, and instances that are not ready must not join the service and should be replaced if preparation fails. System startup is complete. Which control should be used?

choices.text: Configure only a termination lifecycle hook.
choices.explanation: This does not control the instance before it joins the service during launch.

choices.text: Use Pending:Wait in a launch hook to retrieve the settings, return CONTINUE on success, and return ABANDON on failure.
choices.explanation: The instance proceeds only when preparation succeeds.

choices.text: Extend the health check grace period and do not report preparation status.
choices.explanation: The grace period delays replacement decisions but does not control service participation based on a preparation-success notification.

choices.text: Increase the group's minimum capacity and send traffic to instances before preparation is complete.
choices.explanation: This provides additional capacity but cannot make each instance's preparation status a condition.

source.label: EC2 Auto Scalingのライフサイクルフック

learning.reason: A launch lifecycle hook can hold an instance before it enters the service.
learning.concept: When preparation succeeds during the wait, the instance can continue; when it fails, the instance can be abandoned.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Prevent overload on the few targets in one Availability Zone
prompt: An ALB has one target in one Availability Zone and three targets of the same capacity in another Availability Zone. Cross-zone load balancing is disabled for the target group, and the number of requests entering each Availability Zone is similar. The requirement is for each healthy target to receive approximately the same number of requests, and cross-zone distribution is acceptable. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Leave cross-zone load balancing disabled for the target group and shorten the health check interval.
choices.explanation: This does not change the difference in the number of healthy targets or the restriction to distributing requests within each Availability Zone.

choices.text: Enable cookie stickiness in both Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Keeping the same user on an existing target does not distribute requests across Availability Zones.

choices.text: Enable cross-zone load balancing for the target group.
choices.explanation: Each ALB node can distribute requests to targets across all enabled Availability Zones.

choices.text: Move the listener rule to a higher priority.
choices.explanation: Rule priority determines which target group receives traffic; it does not change cross-zone distribution within the same target group.

source.label: ALBターゲットグループのクロスゾーン設定

learning.reason: When distribution is restricted to each Availability Zone, the requests entering that zone are divided among the number of targets in that zone.
learning.concept: To distribute requests across the entire group, configure the target group to use cross-zone load balancing.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Separate standby failover capacity from routine read capacity
prompt: An RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance is in use. The operations team wants to keep the synchronous standby unchanged while offloading aggregation SQL read traffic that can tolerate some staleness to a separate system. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Convert the existing Multi-AZ instance to Single-AZ and then enable aggregation.
choices.explanation: This removes the specified failover protection and does not add a destination for aggregation queries.

choices.text: Inspect the synchronous standby host directly and have aggregation clients always connect to it.
choices.explanation: The synchronous standby of a DB instance deployment does not serve read traffic.

choices.text: Use only the existing primary endpoint, increase the number of connections, and have them distributed to the standby.
choices.explanation: The primary endpoint does not distribute aggregation read requests to the standby.

choices.text: Keep the existing Multi-AZ deployment and create a separate read replica, directing aggregation clients to its endpoint.
choices.explanation: This preserves standby-based availability while isolating aggregation load on an asynchronous replica.

source.label: RDS Multi-AZ DBインスタンスのスタンバイ

learning.reason: The standby of an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance cannot be used as a read-oriented read replica.
learning.concept: High availability and horizontal read scaling require different configurations.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Copy backups to a recovery-only account in the same organization
prompt: A company wants to periodically copy the corresponding EBS backups from a production account to a separate account in the same AWS Organizations organization. The organization's cross-account backup configuration and permissions for the relevant key are already in place, and the source role can initiate the copy. Which additional setting is required in the destination vault?

choices.text: In the destination vault access policy, allow backup:CopyIntoBackupVault for the source account.
choices.explanation: This allows recovery points to be written to the destination vault from the source account.

choices.text: Give the destination vault the same name as the source vault.
choices.explanation: Matching names do not grant permission to copy from another account.

choices.text: Make the existing destination vault public so that it accepts copies from any account without permission settings.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to grant the required permission to a specific copy source.

choices.text: Grant only backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint to the source role.
choices.explanation: Adding delete permission does not change the destination vault's acceptance policy.

source.label: AWS Backupのクロスアカウントコピー

learning.reason: The destination backup vault must use a resource policy to allow copies from another account.
learning.concept: Permission to copy and permission to delete backups in the destination are separate permissions.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Periodically verify that backups can actually be restored
prompt: Scheduled AWS Backup backups are succeeding, but an audit requires periodically restoring the target resources and recording the success status and elapsed time. Temporary resources for validation can be created, and the corresponding resources will be targeted. Which operation should be used?

choices.text: Export recovery-point metadata to CSV daily and treat the size of each file as its restore time.
choices.explanation: File size alone does not show whether restoration succeeds or how long the actual restoration takes.

choices.text: Increase the backup plan's execution frequency and report the latest successful backup as a successful restore.
choices.explanation: A restore must be performed and its result verified separately from creating a recovery point.

choices.text: Configure the scope and frequency in a restore testing plan, then review the execution results and job duration.
choices.explanation: This performs actual restores and allows the testing cycle and records to be reproduced.

choices.text: Extend the backup retention period and omit validation of the restore procedure.
choices.explanation: This expands the range of historical backups that can be retained, but does not provide evidence of successful restores.

source.label: AWS Backupの復元テスト

learning.reason: Successful creation of a recovery point does not prove that recovery succeeds within the required time; that must be verified separately.
learning.concept: A restore testing plan selects recovery points and runs restore jobs.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Set a requirement for replication time for new objects
prompt: New audit files are stored in versioned Amazon S3 and replicated to another Region with CRR. A standard replication configuration is in place, but a service level is now required for replicating most future new objects within 15 minutes, along with observation of data that is delayed. What should be configured?

choices.text: Specify the same storage class for the destination and simply wait for delivery.
choices.explanation: The destination storage class does not add an SLA for replication within 15 minutes.

choices.text: Run S3 Batch Replication on all objects once every hour.
choices.explanation: Repeated batch replication does not provide a 15-minute SLA for new files.

choices.text: Set the CloudFront TTL to 15 minutes so that S3 objects can be read more easily.
choices.explanation: A cache refresh interval does not manage the replication time for CRR.

choices.text: Enable S3 Replication Time Control on the applicable CRR rule.
choices.explanation: This applies a replication time objective and metrics to new objects.

source.label: S3 Replication Time Control

learning.reason: When a replication time target and observation of delays are required, S3 Replication Time Control can be used.
learning.concept: Standard replication is asynchronous, while S3 Replication Time Control provides an SLA for replicating new objects within 15 minutes.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Expire only older versions while retaining the current version
prompt: In a versioning-enabled S3 bucket, older versions of frequently updated data are accumulating. The current version and the three most recent noncurrent versions must be retained, while any earlier noncurrent version should be automatically deleted after it has been noncurrent for more than 90 days. Which rule should be used?

choices.text: Disable versioning within 90 days of each object's creation time.
choices.explanation: This cannot automatically manage the number or age of existing noncurrent versions.

choices.text: Set NoncurrentVersionExpiration in a rule with a filter, with NoncurrentDays set to 90 and NewerNoncurrentVersions set to 3.
choices.explanation: Only older noncurrent versions that meet both conditions expire, while the current version and the three most recent noncurrent versions are retained.

choices.text: Configure only the transition of noncurrent versions and move them to a lower-cost class.
choices.explanation: This changes storage cost but does not delete noncurrent versions.

choices.text: Set Expiration Days to 90 and expire current objects without specifying a version-retention count.
choices.explanation: The current version would become unavailable, and the requirement to retain the three most recent versions is not specified.

source.label: S3 Lifecycleと非現行バージョンの失効

learning.reason: For noncurrent versions, both elapsed days and the number of newer versions to retain can be specified.
learning.concept: A rule that expires current versions and deletion specifically for noncurrent versions are separate actions.

sourceLabel: S3 Lifecycle and expiration of noncurrent versions

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Switch DNS responses to the healthy Region
prompt: Traffic should normally go to a public ALB in the primary Region and switch to a secondary Region only when the service cannot be provided in the primary Region. Each of the two ALBs has one target group for this service. Without adding external health checks, the switch must use the status of the existing targets. Which settings are required? Choose two.

choices.text: Include both in responses from the start with equal weights during healthy operation.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the requirement to prioritize only the primary during normal operation.

choices.text: Register both under simple routing with the same priority and perform inter-Region forwarding only on the ALB side.
choices.explanation: Simple routing does not configure this primary-secondary failover based on health.

choices.text: Shorten the TTL only for the primary record and have an administrator register the secondary during an outage.
choices.explanation: The switch depends on manual action and does not automatically evaluate target health.

choices.text: Create two failover aliases with the same FQDN and configure one as primary and the other as secondary.
choices.explanation: This configures routing that prioritizes the primary during normal operation.

choices.text: Enable Evaluate Target Health for both aliases.
choices.explanation: This allows the target status of the ALBs to be used for the failover decision.

source.label: Route 53のエイリアス先の状態評価

learning.reason: In an active-passive configuration, assign primary and secondary failover records to the same name.
learning.concept: Using Evaluate Target Health with ELB aliases allows Route 53 to refer to target health.

sourceLabel: Health evaluation for Route 53 alias targets

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Separate a shared file service from a single AZ
prompt: An existing Linux application uses an NFS shared file system. It requires NetApp ONTAP compatibility and must continue serving from another AZ if an AZ failure occurs in the same Region. The application cannot be modified to rewrite the shared-file destination during a failure. Which deployment should be used?

choices.text: Choose an FSx for ONTAP Multi-AZ deployment and connect to the file system from the NFS client.
choices.explanation: If a failure occurs in the preferred AZ, an automatic failover to the standby AZ occurs.

choices.text: Create daily backups and restore them in the same AZ after a failure occurs.
choices.explanation: This depends on the failed AZ and cannot keep the service running during the failure.

choices.text: Create the file system in a Single-AZ deployment and add more subnets in the same AZ.
choices.explanation: Adding subnets within the same AZ does not protect against an outage of the entire AZ.

choices.text: Create two independent Single-AZ file systems in separate locations and copy files only at night.
choices.explanation: This provides neither write synchronization nor automatic failover, and the application would also need its connection destination updated.

source.label: FSx for ONTAPのSingle-AZとMulti-AZ配置

learning.reason: A Multi-AZ deployment places file servers in a preferred AZ and a standby AZ.
learning.concept: Depending on the configuration, clients using the share can use service-managed failover.

sourceLabel: FSx for ONTAP Single-AZ and Multi-AZ deployments

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Prepare replacement capacity before waiting for an interruption notice
prompt: Spot workers in an EC2 Auto Scaling group are experiencing more interruptions during execution. You want to try launching replacement instances first when EC2 reports an increased interruption risk, even before the two-minute interruption notice is issued. The workers can already stop jobs safely. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Enable Capacity Rebalancing for the group.
choices.explanation: When an increased interruption risk recommendation is received, it attempts to launch new Spot Instances first.

choices.text: Set a low threshold in a target tracking policy for CPU utilization.
choices.explanation: Scaling instance count based on CPU load does not process interruption-risk notifications.

choices.text: Only extend the wait time through an instance lifecycle hook.
choices.explanation: A launch or termination hook is not a setting that attempts replacement in response to a rebalancing recommendation.

choices.text: Increase the maximum Spot price and stop receiving increased-risk notifications.
choices.explanation: Pricing alone does not launch replacement instances in response to a rebalancing recommendation.

source.label: EC2 Auto Scalingのキャパシティーリバランス

learning.reason: When a rebalancing recommendation is received, the group attempts replacement early.
learning.concept: Proactive replacement based on interruption risk is a different decision from scaling instance count when load increases.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Ensure full-block performance immediately after restoring from a backup
prompt: There is a drill to restore an EBS snapshot to a specific AZ in the Osaka Region. You need the required performance from the first read of the new volume. There is no time to initialize the entire volume by reading it, and the target snapshot and AZ are known in advance. Which preparation is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore for the target snapshot in the target AZ, then create the volume after it becomes available and its creation credits are ready.
choices.explanation: When creation credits are available in the target AZ, a volume with all blocks initialized can be created.

choices.text: Create the volume with a standard restore, then enable Fast Snapshot Restore for the snapshot.
choices.explanation: Fast Snapshot Restore does not apply retroactively to a volume that has already been created.

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore in a different AZ and create the volume in the planned AZ.
choices.explanation: Because the enabled AZ does not match, the volume is not covered by fast restoration.

choices.text: Enable only detailed monitoring for the instance metrics and restore the volume.
choices.explanation: Increasing metric observation frequency does not change initialization for the first data read.

source.label: EBSの高速スナップショット復元

learning.reason: Fast Snapshot Restore is enabled for a snapshot and an AZ combination.
learning.concept: It reduces initialization latency for new volumes created in that AZ from the enabled snapshot.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Maintain common settings after startup, including on new servers
prompt: You want to install a monitoring agent on managed EC2 instances with the same tag and periodically return them to the desired state after configuration changes. Future targets must be applied automatically, without an operator sending a run command each time. Which service should you use?

choices.text: Keep an interactive operator session open with Session Manager.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for periodic application without depending on manual action.

choices.text: Run Run Command once and specify the current list of managed nodes.
choices.explanation: This processes only the initial targets and does not track nodes that join later or configuration changes.

choices.text: Update the agent configuration through a Patch Manager scan.
choices.explanation: Checking patch compliance cannot be used to continuously apply the configuration of a custom application.

choices.text: Prepare an SSM document for the configuration and create a State Manager association that targets the tag and repeats the application on a schedule.
choices.explanation: The configuration can be continuously applied to target managed nodes, including new nodes with the same tag.

source.label: Systems Manager State Manager

learning.reason: A State Manager association continuously applies a document to targets selected by tags.
learning.concept: A one-time command and a desired state maintained on a schedule serve different purposes.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Inspect Patch Status Before Obtaining Change Approval
prompt: In production Linux operations, first count the patches currently missing relative to the approved baseline. During the investigation, do not update packages or reboot the system. In accordance with the change policy, perform the installation later as a separate task. Which Patch Manager operation should be used?

choices.text: Run the operation with Operation set to Install and RebootOption set to NoReboot.
choices.explanation: This can suppress an automatic reboot, but the patches will still be installed.

choices.text: Run AWS-RunPatchBaseline on the targets with Operation set to Scan, and check their compliance status.
choices.explanation: This compares the targets with the baseline to identify missing patches without installing them.

choices.text: Run the operating system's update command and observe which packages change.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to investigate without changing packages.

choices.text: Reject all patches in the baseline and use Install to produce the investigation results.
choices.explanation: This does not identify missing items against the actual baseline intended for approval.

source.label: AWS-RunPatchBaselineのScanとInstall

learning.reason: A scan reports patch compliance status, while installation applies patches. AWS-RunPatchBaseline supports separating the inventory needed for an apply decision from the later installation step.
learning.concept: Inventory needed to decide whether to apply patches can be performed separately from installation.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Stop Distribution to Remaining Nodes After a Small Number of Failures
prompt: You are distributing a configuration update to multiple EC2 instances with Systems Manager Run Command. Let nodes that are already running continue to completion, but stop sending the command to remaining nodes when the operational failure threshold is exceeded. The limit on the number of instances processed concurrently is already configured. Which parameter should you specify?

choices.text: Separate the S3 output destinations and store logs from failed nodes separately.
choices.explanation: This helps investigate failures, but it does not stop distribution to the remaining instances.

choices.text: Set MaxErrors so that new distribution stops when the number of failures exceeds the allowed value.
choices.explanation: This suppresses sending to remaining targets without uniformly canceling operations that are already running.

choices.text: Shorten the execution timeout for every command.
choices.explanation: This sets a deadline for each execution; it does not specify stopping new distribution after some executions fail.

choices.text: Reduce only MaxConcurrency to half its current value.
choices.explanation: This reduces parallelism, but it does not configure stopping based on the number of failures.

source.label: Run Commandのエラー上限

learning.reason: MaxConcurrency and MaxErrors separately control the number of nodes processed in parallel and the number of failures allowed.
learning.concept: When the error limit is exceeded, the nodes affected are those to which the command has not yet been newly sent.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Do Not Start New Tasks Near the End of a Maintenance Window
prompt: An SSM Maintenance Window starts at 01:00 on Sunday and lasts four hours. You must not forcibly stop tasks that are already running, but you want to avoid starting new tasks from 04:00 onward, one hour before the window ends. The targets and tasks are already registered. How should you configure it?

choices.text: Set the duration to four hours and Cutoff to four hours.
choices.explanation: This leaves almost no time in which tasks can start and does not preserve the required first three hours.

choices.text: Keep the maintenance window duration at four hours and set Cutoff to one hour.
choices.explanation: No new tasks will start during the final hour before the window closes.

choices.text: Set the execution time of every task to one hour.
choices.explanation: Changing individual deadlines does not uniformly prevent new tasks from starting from 04:00 onward.

choices.text: Set the execution-side concurrency to one and leave Cutoff unchanged.
choices.explanation: Running tasks one at a time does not prevent a new task from starting immediately before the window closes.

source.label: SSM Maintenance Windowsのcutoff

learning.reason: Cutoff is the amount of time before a maintenance window closes during which new tasks can no longer start.
learning.concept: Distinguish the period during which tasks may start from the handling of individual tasks that have already started.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Deploy Monitoring Configuration When Accounts Join a Department OU
prompt: Create the same CloudFormation notification topic and monitoring role in every account in a specific Organizations OU. Trusted access with the organization is enabled, and you also want deployment to occur automatically when a new account is added to the OU. Which configuration should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Use self-managed permissions to enumerate the current account IDs, and do not change the StackSet targets when accounts are added.
choices.explanation: New accounts that join the OU cannot be automatically included in the deployment targets.

choices.text: Share the template through S3 and have the account creator create it from the console as needed.
choices.explanation: This provides neither automatic deployment when an account joins the OU nor continued management of the same configuration.

choices.text: Use a StackSet with service-managed permissions and specify the target OU and Regions.
choices.explanation: The organization's OU can be managed as the deployment target.

choices.text: Create a CloudFormation Export from a regular stack in the management account and wait for resources in other accounts to be created automatically.
choices.explanation: An Export is used to reference values; it does not create stacks in other accounts.

choices.text: Enable automatic deployment on the target StackSet.
choices.explanation: When a new account joins the OU, deployment of the required stack is initiated.

source.label: CloudFormation StackSetsの自動デプロイ

learning.reason: CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions can target organizational OUs and perform automatic deployment.
learning.concept: This manages stack instances based on changes to OU membership rather than manually deploying to individual accounts.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Retain the Previous Version of a Database Replaced During an Update
prompt: An RDS DB instance must be replaced during a CloudFormation update. According to the operating policy, the old instance must not be deleted immediately after the replacement; it will be handled separately after the comparison is complete. The stack is not currently scheduled for deletion. Which attribute should be configured?

choices.text: Enable only termination protection for the stack.
choices.explanation: This feature restricts stack deletion; it does not control physical resource replacement caused by an authorized update.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain on the DB resource, and perform the update that requires replacement.
choices.explanation: The new DB becomes the managed resource, while the physical DB that was replaced can remain without being deleted.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Snapshot and continue using the old DB connection as is.
choices.explanation: This retains a snapshot but not the old DB itself, and it does not meet the requirement to connect to it immediately for comparison.

choices.text: Set only the DB's DeletionPolicy to Retain and do not specify UpdateReplacePolicy.
choices.explanation: The setting for handling the old DB created by an update replacement is not configured as required.

source.label: CloudFormation UpdateReplacePolicy

learning.reason: For a replacement caused by an update, UpdateReplacePolicy specifies how to handle the old physical resource.
learning.concept: Its applicability differs from DeletionPolicy, which controls handling when the stack is deleted or the resource is removed from the template.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Retain Successfully Provisioned Resources After a Dependency Failure
prompt: In a new validation CloudFormation stack, only the final resource fails with a configuration error and reaches CREATE_FAILED. You want to retain the other resources that were already created for investigation, fix the cause, and then continue from that point. Which failure option should you select during the initial creation?

choices.text: Select Preserve successfully provisioned resources before starting the creation.
choices.explanation: This retains resources that were already created and allows you to fix the issue from CREATE_FAILED.

choices.text: Use the setting that deletes the stack on failure.
choices.explanation: The successfully created resources that you want to retain for investigation will also become targets of the deletion process.

choices.text: Add DeletionPolicy with a value of Retain only to the failed resource that is pending.
choices.explanation: This is not the general failure-time setting used to retain other resources that succeeded before the failure.

choices.text: Perform the normal creation rollback and use CloudTrail to connect to the deleted resources.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records remain, but they cannot be used to investigate with resources that have already been deleted.

source.label: CloudFormationのスタック失敗オプション

learning.reason: The option to retain successfully provisioned resources configures the stack not to roll back when creation fails.
learning.concept: You can inspect the cause while keeping successfully created resources, then retry or update afterward.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Replace Manual OS Image Updates with a Recurring Process
prompt: Every month, a team applies OS patches and common monitoring software to an approved base AMI. Only AMIs that pass smoke tests should be distributed. Which combination of settings should be used to automate the manual instance-preparation process? Select two.

choices.text: Prepare an image recipe that defines the base AMI and the components used for modification and validation.
choices.explanation: This fixes the content of the build and test process.

choices.text: Configure a monthly schedule and image distribution targets in an Image Builder pipeline that uses the recipe.
choices.explanation: This manages recurring execution and distribution of images that succeed.

choices.text: Schedule monthly EBS snapshot creation and treat successful snapshot creation as the OS smoke test.
choices.explanation: Successful disk storage is different from testing whether the application starts.

choices.text: Use only User Data in a launch template to apply updates after startup to each production instance.
choices.explanation: This does not create and distribute a common AMI that has been tested on a recurring schedule.

choices.text: Temporarily increase the minimum size of the Auto Scaling group each month and treat those instances as a new AMI.
choices.explanation: Adjusting capacity alone does not create or distribute an image.

source.label: EC2 Image Builderのイメージパイプライン

learning.reason: An image recipe's build and test process can be run on a recurring basis as a pipeline.
learning.concept: The definition can include both the changes to be applied and the existing distribution targets, and the result of each execution can be tracked.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Insert Operator Approval During a Recovery Procedure
prompt: A standard Systems Manager Automation runbook first collects the state of production and then changes the configuration. The change should be performed only after two approvers review the state-collection output and approve it. Which method avoids requiring an operator to manually start a separate runbook?

choices.text: Run state collection and aws:approve after the configuration change.
choices.explanation: The configuration has already changed when approval is requested, so this does not control the change beforehand.

choices.text: Place aws:approve after state collection and before the change, and configure the permitted approvers and MinRequiredApprovals to 2.
choices.explanation: The configuration-change step does not proceed until the two permitted approvers have approved.

choices.text: Use SNS to notify the operators and proceed when delivery succeeds, treating delivery as approval.
choices.explanation: Successful notification delivery is different from confirmation by an approver.

choices.text: Set the Automation concurrency to 2 and treat the start of two executions as approval.
choices.explanation: This setting controls concurrency and does not record an operator's decision.

source.label: Systems Manager Automationのaws:approve

learning.reason: aws:approve can pause a runbook partway through execution and wait for the required number of approvals.
learning.concept: Placing approval between state collection and the change allows the decision to use information from the same execution.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Increase the EC2 foundation for ECS tasks waiting for capacity
prompt: When you increase the number of tasks in ECS on EC2, deployment of the software waits because there are not enough available resources. The cluster has an Auto Scaling group. You want ECS to adjust the capacity of the underlying EC2 instances to match the service's desired task count. What should you configure?

choices.text: Increase only the ECS service's desired task count and keep the group's size fixed.
choices.explanation: The number of tasks to run increases, but the EC2 capacity available to place them does not.

choices.text: Treat the CPU reservation of ECS tasks as zero and place all tasks on the same host.
choices.explanation: This does not increase physical capacity and does not correctly reserve the resources required by the tasks.

choices.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group as an ECS capacity provider, enable Managed Scaling, and use it with the target service.
choices.explanation: The group's capacity can be adjusted when there is not enough capacity to place the tasks.

choices.text: Switch to an AWS Fargate capacity provider and have it manage the Auto Scaling of the existing EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Fargate has no capability to scale the target EC2 group up or down.

source.label: ECSのクラスターAuto Scaling

learning.reason: Managed Scaling for an EC2 capacity provider adjusts the capacity of the container instances required.
learning.concept: Service Auto Scaling changes the number of tasks, whereas cluster Auto Scaling changes the number of underlying instances.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Import a manually created bucket into a stack later
prompt: A business S3 bucket is being operated as it was created in the console. While preserving the bucket name and data, you want to manage its configuration in an existing CloudFormation stack going forward. S3 buckets support import, and the bucket is not currently managed by another stack. What should you do next?

choices.text: Declare the bucket in the template with the correct properties and DeletionPolicy, specify the bucket name, and execute an Import change set.
choices.explanation: This associates the existing resource with the stack without replacing it.

choices.text: Apply a normal update that includes creating a bucket with the same name and wait for CloudFormation to adopt it automatically when the existing name conflicts.
choices.explanation: A normal create request does not import an existing bucket into CloudFormation management.

choices.text: Delete the existing bucket and create a new one with the same name.
choices.explanation: Even if the name can be reused, this does not preserve the existing data and continuous use.

choices.text: Treat the bucket as imported simply because the template is complete, without creating a change set.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation does not manage the existing bucket until the import operation is performed.

source.label: CloudFormationの既存スタックへのリソースインポート

learning.reason: Resource Import maps the physical identifier to the template's logical ID.
learning.concept: A normal stack update does not automatically adopt an unregistered physical resource.

sourceLabel: CloudFormation resource import into an existing stack

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Run maintenance progressively from a central location across multiple accounts
prompt: An operations team wants to run one SSM Automation runbook in the target Regions of five accounts, using execution roles that have already been prepared. They need to limit parallel execution across accounts and Regions so that the change does not reach all accounts at once. Which execution settings should they use?

choices.text: Only shorten the maximum session duration of the IAM execution role.
choices.explanation: This controls session length, not the number of locations being worked on concurrently.

choices.text: Specify the accounts, Regions, and execution role in TargetLocations, and limit the number of parallel locations with TargetLocationMaxConcurrency.
choices.explanation: This enables central control of the same runbook while narrowing the scope changed at the same time.

choices.text: Only limit the number of concurrent executions on nodes in the management account and do not specify the target accounts.
choices.explanation: This does not create an execution path to the five accounts and target Regions.

choices.text: Copy the runbook to S3 and have each account start it manually at the same time without specifying a schedule.
choices.explanation: There is no central control or location-level parallel limit, so the order of changes cannot be managed.

source.label: Systems Manager Automationの複数アカウント実行

learning.reason: Automation target locations let you select accounts and Regions and control execution.
learning.concept: When applying a change across an organization, explicitly specify the targets and concurrency limits at the account and Region level.

sourceLabel: Systems Manager Automation across multiple accounts

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Collect configuration changes from all accounts through the same audit path
prompt: You want to centrally store IAM and EC2 management events from all accounts in an Organization. New members should be added automatically, and individual members must not be able to disable central history collection. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Open Event History in each account and have each user save CSV files as desired.
choices.explanation: This provides neither continuous central storage nor automatic application to new members.

choices.text: Share CloudWatch EC2 instance metrics centrally.
choices.explanation: This provides access to performance metrics but does not record the execution history of AWS management APIs.

choices.text: Create a standard trail only in the management account and give it the same name as the organization's bucket.
choices.explanation: The trail's scope is not expanded across the organization by the bucket name.

choices.text: As the management account or a delegated administrator, create a multi-Region organization trail and deliver management events to a central S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: It can be applied automatically to new members, and members cannot disable the organization trail.

source.label: CloudTrailの組織証跡

learning.reason: An organization trail applies to member accounts, and members cannot modify the organization trail.
learning.concept: In addition to account-specific Event History viewing, long-term retention can be configured through an organization trail.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Encrypting New EBS Resources While Keeping Existing Workloads Running
prompt: An account has unencrypted EBS resources running in the Tokyo Region. The account must encrypt new EBS volumes created in the same Region and copies of snapshots, even when encryption is omitted from an individual template. Existing disks must not be changed by this effort. Which setting should be configured?

choices.text: Configure only automatic rotation for a customer managed KMS key.
choices.explanation: The key used by encrypted resources can be managed, but this does not enable encryption when new EBS resources are created.

choices.text: Enable EBS encryption by default in the Tokyo Region.
choices.explanation: Resources created in this Region from now on will be encrypted, while existing volumes that are currently running remain unchanged.

choices.text: Enable encryption by default only in Regions other than Tokyo.
choices.explanation: The setting in another Region does not apply to new volumes in Tokyo.

choices.text: Add encryption only to templates that permit new resource creation, while leaving creation through the console and APIs unchanged.
choices.explanation: Creation that does not use a template could still omit the encryption setting.

source.label: EBSのデフォルト暗号化

learning.reason: EBS encryption by default is configured separately for each account and Region.
learning.concept: The setting applies to resources created in the future; it does not change the encryption state of existing resources.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Notify the On-Call Team Based on Severity
prompt: The team wants to deliver only high-severity GuardDuty findings to an on-call SNS topic. Low-severity findings must remain available for investigation in GuardDuty, and a continuously running poller must not be added. What should be configured? Select two.

choices.text: Stop the GuardDuty detector and send notifications only when CloudWatch CPU utilization increases.
choices.explanation: GuardDuty threat findings and their severity would no longer be available.

choices.text: Set the on-call SNS topic as a target of the applicable EventBridge rule.
choices.explanation: Matching events can be delivered through the existing notification path.

choices.text: Hide all low-severity GuardDuty findings and manually post to SNS every day.
choices.explanation: This does not provide automated notification or keep low-severity findings available for investigation.

choices.text: Send all CloudTrail API calls directly to SNS and have SNS calculate the severity.
choices.explanation: SNS does not generate GuardDuty severity from API logs in this way.

choices.text: Configure an EventBridge pattern for GuardDuty Finding events that selects findings whose severity meets the specified condition.
choices.explanation: Only findings matching the configured severity are considered by the rule.

source.label: GuardDutyの検出結果をEventBridgeで受け取る

learning.reason: Findings can be received through EventBridge, and their severity can be used as a matching condition.
learning.concept: Keep finding storage and visibility separate from the question of which severity levels should be sent to whom.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Scan EC2 Instances That Cannot Use a Management Agent
prompt: A security team uses Amazon Inspector to scan EC2 instances running a supported operating system in a required development environment. Some instances cannot establish a management connection through SSM Agent and are also using a supported EBS volume configuration. Which scanning mode should be used?

choices.text: Set the Inspector EC2 scan to hybrid mode and verify that the applicable instances are eligible for agentless scanning.
choices.explanation: Eligible instances can use a scanning path that does not require SSM Agent.

choices.text: Treat the OS package scan as successful if GuardDuty reports zero findings.
choices.explanation: GuardDuty threat detection and Inspector vulnerability scanning serve different purposes.

choices.text: Use agent-based scanning only and treat instances that are not managed through SSM as processed.
choices.explanation: The prerequisites for agent-based scanning are not met, so some instances would remain unscanned.

choices.text: Apply an Inspector exclusion tag to eligible instances to force a normal scan.
choices.explanation: An exclusion tag removes instances from scanning; it does not enable agentless scanning.

source.label: Amazon InspectorのEC2スキャンモード

learning.reason: Hybrid scanning can scan eligible instances through an agentless path when an agent is unavailable.
learning.concept: Eligibility as a scan target is separate from whether the instance can use an agent-based method through an SSM connection.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Suppress Known Exceptions Under Defined Conditions During an Audit Period
prompt: The team wants to automatically suppress only the findings aggregated by AWS Security Hub CSPM that have an audit-approved exception tag. The rule must also apply to matching findings that arrive later, while scanning for other configurations continues. What should be configured?

choices.text: Include suppressed in the name of the IAM role used for authentication.
choices.explanation: A role name does not change the workflow of findings.

choices.text: Unsubscribe only from the SNS notification and automatically update the workflow status on the Security Hub side.
choices.explanation: Stopping external notifications does not suppress findings in Security Hub.

choices.text: Specify the exception conditions for the applicable controls and resources in an automation rule, and update the workflow status to SUPPRESSED.
choices.explanation: Only matching findings are suppressed, while other findings continue to be evaluated.

choices.text: Disable all controls in the applicable standard, stopping the other controls in the same standard as well.
choices.explanation: This cannot limit the change to specific approved exceptions.

source.label: Security Hub CSPMのオートメーションルール

learning.reason: An automation rule can update a finding's Workflow status based on matching conditions.
learning.concept: Disabling control evaluation and operationally suppressing individual findings are different actions.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Temporarily stop new cryptographic operations during an investigation and resume them later
prompt: An operations team wants to temporarily stop use of a customer managed KMS key while investigating whether the key is being used for its intended purpose. After the investigation, the team will reuse the same key for decryption and does not plan to delete it. Which operation should the team perform?

choices.text: Use ScheduleKeyDeletion to schedule deletion for the shortest available period, then run EnableKey after the deletion deadline is reached.
choices.explanation: After deletion is completed, the same key cannot be enabled again.

choices.text: Only change the automatic rotation interval to stop all cryptographic operations.
choices.explanation: The rotation configuration does not disable use of the key.

choices.text: Disable the key with DisableKey, then enable the same key with EnableKey after the investigation.
choices.explanation: This temporarily stops use without scheduling deletion and allows the same key to be reused for cryptographic operations after the investigation.

choices.text: Delete only the key alias while continuing to allow use of the key ARN.
choices.explanation: Cryptographic operations that specify the key ARN are not stopped by deleting only the alias.

source.label: AWS KMSキーの有効化・無効化

learning.reason: A customer managed key can be temporarily taken out of use by disabling it and later returned to use by enabling it.
learning.concept: During an investigation, also verify how services that use cached data keys behave.

sourceLabel: Enabling and disabling AWS KMS keys

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Prevent even administrators from deleting an object until its retention date
prompt: Legal requires a specific version of an object in a versioned S3 bucket to be protected from deletion or shortening of its active retention period by privileged users in the account until the retention period expires. The retention date has already been determined. Which S3 Object Lock setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Retain the object in governance mode and grant bypass permissions to the required users.
choices.explanation: Users with bypass permissions could delete the object early, so this does not protect it from privileged users.

choices.text: Retain the target version in compliance mode and set the specified date and time.
choices.explanation: The protection applies until the retention period ends, including against the root user.

choices.text: Enable versioning only.
choices.explanation: Versioning can retain previous versions, but it does not prevent authorized users from deleting individual versions.

choices.text: Set only a lifecycle expiration rule.
choices.explanation: This determines when automatic deletion occurs, but it does not prevent manual deletion until the retention period ends.

source.label: S3 Object Lockのコンプライアンスモード

learning.reason: In compliance mode, even privileged users cannot delete a retained version or shorten its retention period while the retention is active.
learning.concept: Bypassing governance mode and managing a legal hold with no expiration are separate controls.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Find sharing outside the intended organization
prompt: An operations team wants to continuously detect whether policies on the organization's S3 buckets allow read access to external accounts. The team must find such permissions even when there is no record of actual access from outside the organization, while generally excluding sharing between internal accounts. Which feature should the team use?

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate a policy for the current IAM role based on its usage history.
choices.explanation: This feature generates a policy candidate from actual activity; it is different from detecting external resource sharing.

choices.text: List object names with S3 Inventory and infer permissions for external accounts from the file names.
choices.explanation: A bucket policy's external sharing cannot be determined from file names.

choices.text: Aggregate only successful GetObject events from CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This cannot detect permissions granted by a policy when no access has actually occurred.

choices.text: Use an IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer with the organization as the trusted zone.
choices.explanation: It detects access granted to external principals without relying on execution history.

source.label: IAM Access Analyzerの外部アクセス検出

learning.reason: An external access analyzer analyzes policies and detects resources whose access is allowed outside the trusted zone.
learning.concept: Analyzing granted permissions is different from auditing whether an actual request was made.

sourceLabel: IAM Access Analyzer external access detection

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Deploy audit rule sets and remediation together
prompt: A team wants to deploy a common set of specified Config rules and the remediation actions corresponding to those rules to multiple accounts where AWS Config recording is enabled. The team does not want to create each rule manually in every account. Which mechanism should the team use?

choices.text: Change only the Config recorder settings and inspect the resources that are created.
choices.explanation: Recorder settings change the recording scope, but compliant rules and automatic remediation require a separate configuration.

choices.text: Create only a Config aggregator.
choices.explanation: An aggregator collects recorded results, but it does not deploy rules or remediation to source accounts.

choices.text: Define the rules and remediation in a Config conformance pack and deploy it to the organization's target accounts.
choices.explanation: The selected evaluations and remediation can be deployed together as a consolidated definition.

choices.text: Enable only Security Hub notification rules.
choices.explanation: Notifications may be possible, but this does not create the required set of Config rules and remediation actions.

source.label: AWS Configのコンフォーマンスパック

learning.reason: A conformance pack can define rules and remediation together in one template.
learning.concept: Consistent organizational deployment and visualization of existing results are separate activities.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Point a zone apex name to a dynamic load balancer
prompt: You want to point the apex of the public domain example.com managed in Route 53 to an ALB DNS name. Do not assume fixed IP addresses, and keep the existing www configuration unchanged. The zone apex has SOA and NS records. What should you add?

choices.text: Register the current IP address list obtained from the ALB as fixed A records.
choices.explanation: ALB IP addresses can change, so a fixed list cannot maintain the required behavior.

choices.text: Set the NS record value for example.com to the ALB DNS name.
choices.explanation: NS records identify the authoritative name servers for a zone; they do not specify an application traffic destination.

choices.text: Create an A alias record for example.com and select the ALB as the alias target.
choices.explanation: An alias can be configured at the zone apex, and Route 53 returns the ALB's current addresses.

choices.text: Create a CNAME for example.com that points to the ALB DNS name.
choices.explanation: A CNAME cannot coexist with the existing records at the zone apex.

source.label: Route 53でELBへルーティング

learning.reason: A CNAME cannot be used at the zone apex, so use an alias for the supported AWS resource.
learning.concept: The ALB's IP addresses do not need to be resolved and registered statically by the application.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Resolve names available only inside the corporate network from a VPC
prompt: A VPC is connected to the corporate network through Direct Connect, and the DNS route and security controls are ready. What should you configure so that applications in the VPC send only corp.example queries to the corporate DNS while preserving resolution of existing AWS names? Select two.

choices.text: Clear the DNS suffix and always forward all name resolution to the corporate network.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the condition that the existing AWS name-resolution path must be preserved.

choices.text: Create only an inbound endpoint in the VPC and make no changes to the corporate DNS.
choices.explanation: An inbound endpoint provides a path for external resolvers to query into the VPC.

choices.text: Create corp.example as an empty Route 53 private hosted zone.
choices.explanation: This only manages the name locally and does not forward queries to the existing corporate DNS records.

choices.text: Create an outbound Resolver endpoint for applications to query the corporate DNS.
choices.explanation: This configures an exit path for AWS-side queries to the destination DNS server.

choices.text: Create a Resolver rule that forwards corp.example to the corporate DNS and associate it with the VPC containing the applications.
choices.explanation: The rule forwards queries matching the specified suffix while preserving the other resolution paths.

source.label: Route 53 Resolverのアウトバウンド転送

learning.reason: Use an outbound endpoint for forwarding queries from AWS to an external DNS server.
learning.concept: Associate the forwarding rule for the target DNS suffix with the application's VPC.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Only the return traffic for outbound HTTPS is blocked by the network ACL
prompt: An EC2 client connects over HTTPS to an external fixed IP address. TCP 443 is allowed in the security group's outbound rules, and outbound traffic to destination TCP port 443 is allowed in the subnet network ACL. However, the network ACL denies the return traffic on ingress. The range of ephemeral ports selected by the client's operating system is known. How should you fix this?

choices.text: Allow only destination TCP 443 in the client's inbound network ACL.
choices.explanation: The external response is returned to an ephemeral port on the client, so destination port 443 does not match.

choices.text: Add another outbound allow rule to the security group.
choices.explanation: Even with an outbound allow rule, it cannot override an inbound network ACL deny.

choices.text: Add an inbound network ACL allow rule with the server's fixed IP as the source and the client's ephemeral port range as the destination, using a rule number evaluated before the applicable deny.
choices.explanation: The allow rule is applied first, permitting the connection response to return to the client's ephemeral ports.

choices.text: Assume that the network ACL is stateful, so an allowed outbound request automatically allows the response.
choices.explanation: That automatic return-traffic behavior belongs to security groups; network ACLs require separate evaluation.

source.label: VPCネットワークACLとエフェメラルポート

learning.reason: A stateless network ACL evaluates request and response traffic separately.
learning.concept: The destination of packets returning to the client is the client's ephemeral port, not the server's port 443.

sourceLabel: VPC network ACLs and ephemeral ports

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Reach same-Region S3 without NAT
prompt: A VPC that does not allow internet connectivity contains two private subnets, and EC2 instances in both subnets must use S3 in the same Region. Use the standard S3 Region name and preserve the existing routes. What should you configure?

choices.text: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and associate the route tables used by both subnets.
choices.explanation: A route to the S3 prefix list is added to each route table, allowing access without NAT.

choices.text: Point the default route of both subnets directly to the existing internet gateway.
choices.explanation: Private addresses alone do not provide internet access, and this violates the stated private-routing requirement.

choices.text: Change only the S3 bucket policy while leaving the VPC routing unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing authorization does not provide a network path from the private subnets to the service.

choices.text: Create an S3 gateway endpoint, but associate it only with the route table for the public subnets.
choices.explanation: The routes for the target private subnets would remain unchanged.

source.label: S3のゲートウェイVPCエンドポイント

learning.reason: A gateway endpoint creates an S3 route in the selected route tables.
learning.concept: The endpoint-creation step must be connected with targeting the route tables used by the subnets.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Private Server Fails Only When Updating Externally
prompt: An EC2 instance is in a private subnet and uses IPv4 to reach an external package server. An Elastic IP has been assigned to a public NAT Gateway, but the route table of the subnet containing the NAT Gateway has only the VPC local route. The EC2 route for 0.0.0.0/0 points to the NAT Gateway. What should be changed?

choices.text: Allow inbound SSH to the EC2 instance and leave the NAT route table unchanged.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to the outbound path and only broadens the inbound surface.

choices.text: In the NAT route table, point 0.0.0.0/0 to the same NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: No next hop to the internet is configured, so packets cannot be forwarded outside the VPC.

choices.text: Change the EC2 route for 0.0.0.0/0 to the Internet Gateway while keeping the EC2 private IPv4 address.
choices.explanation: This bypasses NAT translation, and a private IP address alone cannot connect to the internet.

choices.text: Add a route from 0.0.0.0/0 to the VPC Internet Gateway in the route table of the subnet containing the NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: This allows the NAT-translated outbound IPv4 packets to be sent to the internet.

source.label: VPCのパブリックNAT Gatewayの構成

learning.reason: The private side routes to the NAT Gateway, while the public NAT side routes to the Internet Gateway.
learning.concept: The NAT Gateway's Elastic IP does not replace a route that reaches the Internet Gateway.

sourceLabel: Public NAT Gateway configuration in a VPC

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Connectivity Fails When a Shared VPC Is Used as a Transit Path
prompt: VPC A is peered with VPC B, which provides shared services, and VPC B has a separate peering connection with VPC C. The address ranges do not overlap. Routes were configured to use B as the transit destination when A and C communicate with each other, but the traffic cannot reach its destination. What should be added to the design first?

choices.text: Configure the same DNS suffix for A and C.
choices.explanation: This can change name resolution, but it does not add transit capability to the peering configuration.

choices.text: Only add preferred routes to the CIDRs of A and C on B.
choices.explanation: VPC peering remains nontransitive, so traffic cannot be relayed to B's other peering connection.

choices.text: Change the protocol allowed for communication from A to C from TCP to UDP.
choices.explanation: VPC peering's nontransitivity is unrelated to the choice of transport protocol.

choices.text: Create a direct peering connection between A and C, and configure routes to each other's CIDRs and the required communication permissions.
choices.explanation: This creates a directly reachable path between the two VPCs.

source.label: VPCピアリングの非推移性

learning.reason: A VPC peering connection is a direct connection between peers and does not relay traffic to another peering connection.
learning.concept: Add a direct peer or redesign the architecture with transit support and define the required routes.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Use a VPC Endpoint Without Changing the Existing Service Name
prompt: An interface endpoint for a supported AWS service is used from a VPC that has no internet connectivity. The endpoint-specific DNS name works, but the standard regional name used by the existing SDK resolves to a public IP address. VPC DNS resolution and DNS hostnames are enabled. What should be configured without changing the application?

choices.text: Embed a custom endpoint name in the application that connects to the service.
choices.explanation: This allows connection through the custom name but does not satisfy the requirement to leave the existing application unchanged.

choices.text: Enable private DNS for the interface VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: An application using the standard regional name can then connect to the endpoint.

choices.text: Delete the interface endpoint and change the VPC default route to the NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: This avoids the required private connection and does not meet the network requirement.

choices.text: Externally pin the service's standard name to a public IP address and use the same IP inside the VPC.

title: Prevent a New Image Version from Being Affected by the Existing TTL
prompt: Files delivered through CloudFront use a long cache TTL. On every release, the new versions of images and JavaScript must be referenced immediately, while clients that received old HTML must be able to continue reading the old files. How can this be done while avoiding a large number of invalidation operations?

choices.text: Keep the long TTL and change only the S3 metadata of the files.
choices.explanation: Changing metadata alone does not replace the same-key cache that is still valid at the edge.

choices.text: Disable browser caching for all files and continue using the same keys.
choices.explanation: Old HTML could no longer reference the old files, and the long-cache requirement would be lost.

choices.text: Include a content hash in each file name, distribute each version under a separate key, and update the references in the HTML.
choices.explanation: Because the key is different, the new file can be retrieved without evicting the old cache.

choices.text: Overwrite the files with the same names and wait for expiration while retaining the long TTL.
choices.explanation: While the old cache remains valid, old and new versions cannot be referenced separately.

source.label: CloudFrontキャッシュのオブジェクト版管理

learning.reason: Including a version or hash in the file name causes old and new keys to be cached separately.
learning.concept: Put the new references in the new HTML and retain the old files for an appropriate period.

choices.text: Shorten the TTL of the Route 53 record and leave the CloudFront viewer certificate at its default.

choices.text: Specify the ARN of the Tokyo ACM certificate for viewers because it is in the same Region as the origin.
choices.explanation: The Regional requirement differs for the certificate used by the origin and the certificate attached to CloudFront.

choices.text: Add a custom origin header to CloudFront to terminate TLS for cdn.example.com.
choices.explanation: Headers concern HTTP requests to the origin; they do not configure TLS for viewers.

title: Isolating routes between development VPCs while using shared services
prompt: Development VPC A, development VPC B, and a shared VPC are attached to a Transit Gateway. A and B must both connect to the shared services, but A and B must not be able to reach each other through the Transit Gateway. How should the route tables be used?

choices.text: Add only the shared-services route to A and do not add a route from the shared side back to A.
choices.explanation: Without a return route, communication between A and the shared services cannot complete.

choices.text: Associate all attachments with the same route table and propagate the CIDRs of all VPCs.
choices.explanation: This also creates a Transit Gateway route between A and B.

choices.text: Reassign the same CIDR to both A and B so that they cannot communicate with each other.
choices.explanation: This is not a simple isolation policy and prevents the shared VPC from addressing the two VPCs separately.

choices.text: Associate the development attachments with a route table that contains only the route to the shared VPC, and add return routes to A and B in the shared-side route table.
choices.explanation: This avoids giving the development VPCs routes to each other while allowing return traffic with the shared VPC.

learning.reason: The route table associated with an attachment determines the route table used by traffic entering through that attachment.
learning.concept: Separating route propagation destinations lets you independently control the return paths from the shared side and the destinations reachable from the development side.

title: Connecting to VPC private addresses over a dedicated connection
prompt: A Direct Connect connection exists between the on-premises environment and AWS. A virtual private gateway is already attached on the VPC side. What should be configured?

choices.text: Add a Public VIF and treat the private CIDR as a public AWS IP range.
choices.explanation: A Public VIF is for access to public AWS prefixes and does not provide a private path to a VPC.

choices.text: Associate a Transit VIF directly with the VPC's virtual private gateway.
choices.explanation: A Transit VIF is used to connect to a Transit Gateway through a Direct Connect gateway.

choices.text: Configure a Private VIF and connect it to the VPC's virtual private gateway.
choices.explanation: This adds a private connectivity path to the VPC over the existing dedicated connection.

choices.text: Add only an Internet Gateway to the VPC to learn routes from the dedicated-connection side.
choices.explanation: No VIF is configured for the dedicated connection, so this does not provide connectivity to the private CIDR.

source.label: Direct Connect仮想インターフェイスの種類

learning.reason: A private virtual interface is used to connect to private addresses in a VPC.
learning.concept: Even over the same physical connection, the type of virtual interface must match the connectivity target.

title: Suppressing actions during planned maintenance while preserving state notifications
prompt: During a planned overnight shutdown, the infrastructure is stopped and the application's composite alarm enters the ALARM state. A separate alarm representing maintenance is already configured. What should be configured?

choices.text: Unsubscribe the SNS subscriptions and restore them at the end of the month.
choices.explanation: This does not provide automatic control for each maintenance period and affects other notifications.

choices.text: Add a condition to the composite alarm rule that always evaluates to OK during maintenance.
choices.explanation: This changes the alarm's state transitions during maintenance, so the history no longer represents the same conditions.

choices.text: Specify the maintenance alarm as the ActionsSuppressor and configure the required wait and extension periods.
choices.explanation: This controls only the actions while preserving the state of the composite alarm itself.

choices.text: Treat missing data for each metric as normal.
choices.explanation: This does not suppress notifications for a specified period when abnormal values are actually reported.

learning.reason: Keep state evaluation separate from alarm actions.

choices.text: Enable Container Insights with enhanced observability on the cluster and inspect task- and container-level metrics.

title: A lower oldest-message metric does not mean the problem is resolved

choices.text: Conclude that the first failure has been resolved because the queue guarantees strict send order.

choices.text: Conclude that the message was successfully processed and deleted because the metric decreased.
