title: Exclude an Instance With Work in Progress from Normal Scale-In
prompt: Workers in an EC2 Auto Scaling group receive long-running jobs from a queue. Normal scale-in during periods of lower load should continue, but an instance with work in progress must not be selected as a candidate, and it should become a candidate again after processing is complete. The instance can determine its own state. How should this be implemented?

choices.text: Move the instance in use to another Availability Zone without configuring protection.
choices.explanation: Changing the placement does not exclude an instance in use from termination consideration.

choices.text: Configure only EC2 API termination protection on the instance performing the work.
choices.explanation: This does not function as normal scale-in protection for an Auto Scaling group.

choices.text: Enable scale-in protection for the target instance before processing starts and disable it after processing finishes.
choices.explanation: This prevents the instance in progress from being selected for normal scale-in and allows it to return to the candidate pool afterward.

choices.text: Disable health checks for all instances.
choices.explanation: Health determination and scale-in selection are separate, so a healthy instance could still be selected.

source.label: Amazon EC2 Auto Scalingの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Scale-in protection can be switched for each individual instance.
learning.concept: Protection is intended for normal scale-in; it does not prevent replacement or stopping of unhealthy instances in general.

sourceLabel: Official Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling documentation

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Allow Existing Long-Running HTTP Requests to Complete During a Deployment Update
prompt: During an update, old instances behind an ALB are deregistered one at a time. Processing for existing clients can take up to 90 seconds. After deregistration begins, new requests should be sent elsewhere, while in-flight requests should be given up to 120 seconds to complete. What should be adjusted?

choices.text: Set deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds to 120.
choices.explanation: The target enters the draining state, allowing existing requests to complete within the configured time.

choices.text: Set the health check interval to 120 seconds.
choices.explanation: This is the interval for liveness checks and does not provide a grace period for requests during deregistration.

choices.text: Forcefully terminate EC2 immediately before deregistration.
choices.explanation: This does not give in-flight requests time to finish.

choices.text: Configure only sticky sessions when launching the ALB.
choices.explanation: This fixes the route for the same user and is not the waiting period for draining.

source.label: Elastic Load Balancingの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The draining period during deregistration is managed at the target group.
learning.concept: Switching new traffic and waiting for existing connections to finish are separate concerns.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Promote the replica with sufficient capacity first
prompt: Aurora has a small analytics replica and a replica comparable to the production writer in different Availability Zones. If the writer fails, you want the production-equivalent instance to be promoted first when both are healthy. What should you specify?

choices.text: Add the analytics replica endpoint to DNS and specify promotion based on the endpoint order.
choices.explanation: Registering a connection target does not change the cluster's promotion order.

choices.text: Disable the writer's CPU alarm so that the analytics replica is not promoted.
choices.explanation: Alarm behavior does not control Aurora's promotion priority.

choices.text: Set a smaller Promotion Tier on the production-equivalent replica than on the analytics replica.
choices.explanation: This gives the production-equivalent instance promotion priority among the available candidates.

choices.text: Set a larger Promotion Tier only on the production-equivalent replica.
choices.explanation: This gives it lower priority, which is the opposite of the required behavior.

source.label: Amazon RDSの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Control the promotion order with the instance's Promotion Tier.
learning.concept: A smaller number has higher promotion priority, independently of the replica's normal connection destination.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Limit database connections during a serverless burst
prompt: Several hundred Lambda execution environments send short SQL statements to the same RDS database. You cannot easily increase the database's maximum connection count, and you need to reduce the number of physical connections created per request. The application can change its connection destination, and transactions can be kept short. What should you deploy?

choices.text: Increase Lambda's concurrency limit and keep direct connections to the database.
choices.explanation: Increasing the number of execution environments does not share physical database connections.

choices.text: Connect RDS Proxy to the target database and point Lambda to the proxy endpoint.
choices.explanation: It can pool and reuse database connections, absorbing a sudden increase in client connections.

choices.text: Use Multi-AZ for the database and use the standby as a connection pool.
choices.explanation: Adding a standby does not consolidate client connections.

choices.text: Increase the Lambda timeout and create a new database connection for each execution.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce physical connection consumption and may hold connections longer.

source.label: Amazon RDSの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Use a pool to separate logical connections from database clients and physical connections to the database.
learning.concept: Long transactions or session pinning reduce multiplexing efficiency.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Allow time for restoration from long-term storage
prompt: A snapshot of old EBS audit data is in the archive tier. You plan to create a volume for an investigation several days from now and want to use it immediately when the work starts that day. What should you do now?

choices.text: Delete the original backup before restoring it to the standard tier.
choices.explanation: This would lose the recovery point needed for the planned investigation.

choices.text: Restore the archived snapshot to the standard tier, temporarily or permanently, and create the volume after the restoration is complete.
choices.explanation: After the snapshot is returned to an available state, it can be used to create the resource.

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore only in another Availability Zone while keeping the snapshot in the archive tier.
choices.explanation: Enabling Fast Snapshot Restore alone does not retrieve a snapshot from the archive tier.

choices.text: Run CreateVolume while the snapshot remains in the archive tier and assume it will be usable immediately.
choices.explanation: The snapshot must first be restored to the standard tier.

source.label: Amazon EBSの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Restore a snapshot in the archive tier to the standard tier before using it.
learning.concept: The restoration wait time can be included in the work schedule.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Restore the setting that stopped continuous backup
prompt: AWS Backup continuous backup for S3 has stopped. Versioning and the backup role are enabled, but just before the failure, event delivery from the S3 bucket to Amazon EventBridge was disabled. Without modifying a custom application, you need to recover the record of future changes. What should you do first?

choices.text: Disable versioning and then rerun the same continuous backup.
choices.explanation: This removes a setting required for continuous backup and does not restore delivery of change events.

choices.text: Generate S3 Inventory daily and use it as the change events for continuous backup.
choices.explanation: An inventory listing is not an individual change event delivered to EventBridge.

choices.text: Re-enable EventBridge notifications for the bucket, then check the backup plan and continuous job status.
choices.explanation: This restores the supply of change events required for continuous backup.

choices.text: Increase the number of periodic snapshots and treat them as allowing restoration to any time between snapshots.
choices.explanation: This increases the number of periodic recovery points but does not restore the continuous-backup event path.

source.label: AWS Backupの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: S3 continuous backup receives S3 events through EventBridge.
learning.concept: Check both the backup plan and the path that delivers actual object changes.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Restore Part of a Shared File Alongside Existing Data
prompt: A deleted shared directory must be recovered from an EFS file system protected by AWS Backup. The current data in the original file system must not be changed, and the restored content must be verified before the required files are moved back. Which restore option should be used?

choices.text: Copy the metadata displayed in the list of recovery points as the original files.
choices.explanation: Recovery-point metadata is not the file content.

choices.text: Use item-level restore to specify the target path and restore it to the restore directory created in the existing EFS file system.
choices.explanation: The restored data can be verified alongside the existing data, and only the required files can then be moved.

choices.text: Restore the entire file system to the existing EFS file system without selecting a directory during the restore job.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to restore only the target directory.

choices.text: Change the EFS storage class and return all files to the backup point in time.
choices.explanation: Changing a storage class does not restore files.

source.label: AWS Backupの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: EFS item-level restore lets you specify the path to restore.
learning.concept: When restoring to an existing file system, the selected items are placed in a new restore directory under the root.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Provide a Local EFS Mount Target for Tasks in a New AZ
prompt: An ECS service that shares a Regional EFS file system is being expanded to a third AZ in the same VPC. The existing data and file system must remain shared, and clients in the additional AZ must use a mount target in that same AZ. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Align the container name in the ECS task definition with the new AZ.
choices.explanation: Changing a name does not create an EFS mount target in the same AZ.

choices.text: Create an independent EFS file system in the additional AZ and assign it the same file system ID.
choices.explanation: An independent file system does not share the data as-is, and file system IDs are not shared.

choices.text: Delete the target in an existing AZ and move its subnet to the additional AZ.
choices.explanation: A subnet belongs to an AZ, and this would also affect connections from the existing AZ.

choices.text: Create a mount target for the same EFS file system in the additional AZ.
choices.explanation: Clients in the additional AZ can access the same data through a local connection point.

source.label: Amazon EFSの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: For a Regional EFS file system, one mount target can be created in each AZ where it is used.
learning.concept: A mount target is a network connection point to the same EFS file system, not a separate file system.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Automate Promotion When the Cache Primary Node Stops
prompt: An ElastiCache for Redis OSS node-based deployment uses a replication group with cluster mode disabled. If an AZ failure in the Region causes the primary node to stop, a read replica in another AZ must be promoted automatically. Which combination is required? Select two.

choices.text: Place all replicas in the same AZ as the primary.
choices.explanation: The replicas would also be unavailable during a failure of the entire AZ.

choices.text: Place a read replica in another AZ.
choices.explanation: This provides a copy that can be promoted even if the primary node's AZ stops operating.

choices.text: Send writes to a replica and manually switch its role with the primary node.
choices.explanation: This does not provide automatic promotion, and a normal replica is not a write destination.

choices.text: Enable Multi-AZ and automatic failover.
choices.explanation: The service can detect a primary-node failure and promote an available replica.

choices.text: Use only a primary node and take daily snapshots.
choices.explanation: There is no running node in another AZ to promote.

source.label: Amazon ElastiCacheの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Place a replica in another AZ and use a Multi-AZ configuration that includes automatic failover.
learning.concept: Storing snapshots and promoting a node online are different recovery methods.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Move Failed Messages to an Application-Specific DLQ
prompt: A production standard SQS queue must send unprocessable messages to a dedicated DLQ after five receives. The dedicated DLQ must not allow use by source queues belonging to other applications. Which combination should be used? Select two.

choices.text: Set the dedicated DLQ's RedriveAllowPolicy to allowAll.
choices.explanation: Other source queues could also use the dedicated DLQ.

choices.text: In the source queue's RedrivePolicy, specify the dedicated DLQ and set maxReceiveCount to 5.
choices.explanation: Messages that repeatedly fail processing are moved to the specified DLQ after the configured number of receives.

choices.text: Set the DLQ's RedriveAllowPolicy to byQueue and specify only the target source queue.
choices.explanation: This restricts use of the DLQ so that source queues not specified cannot use it.

choices.text: Set the visibility timeout to 5 seconds so messages can be moved under the same condition as the fifth receive.
choices.explanation: The visibility timeout controls how long before a message can be received again; it does not determine the receive count for moving a message.

choices.text: Shorten the source message retention period so expired messages move to the dedicated DLQ.
choices.explanation: Expiration due to the retention period is not DLQ movement caused by the configured receive count.

source.label: Amazon SQSの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Specify the source-side redrive configuration separately from the DLQ-side permissions.
learning.concept: For queues of the same type, messages can be moved using a maximum receive-count threshold.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Switching Reads and Writes to Another Region During a Failure Exercise
prompt: A DynamoDB Global Table uses multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC). The application in Tokyo is stopped and restarted in Osaka, where a replica of the global table already exists. What should be changed to read and write without sending traffic to Tokyo?

choices.text: In the Osaka application, configure the DynamoDB client for the Osaka Region and use the same table name.
choices.explanation: The application can read from and write to the local replica in the active Region.

choices.text: Keep the client configured for the Tokyo endpoint and wait for DynamoDB to forward requests automatically to Osaka.
choices.explanation: The application's Region configuration does not switch automatically.

choices.text: Create a separate table with the same name in Osaka and do not use the replica.
choices.explanation: This loses continued access to the replicated data.

choices.text: Assume that writes in Osaka are impossible unless the Tokyo replica is manually deleted first.
choices.explanation: Replicas in a multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC) configuration can accept writes from each Region.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDBの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A replica in each Region can be accessed through that Region's endpoint.
learning.concept: Cross-Region replication is configured separately from switching the application's connection endpoint.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Stopping New Traffic to Only the Affected Zone Within a Region
prompt: The corresponding ALB and application run in three AZs in the same Region. One AZ is suspected to have failed, and the other AZs have sufficient capacity. The load balancer is registered as an ARC resource and has the required configuration. You need to avoid new traffic to the affected AZ for a limited time. What should you start?

choices.text: Disable the targets in all AZs temporarily.
choices.explanation: This also stops processing in healthy AZs and prevents the service from continuing.

choices.text: Reissue only the certificate for the affected ALB.
choices.explanation: This does not change the conditions for zonal traffic shifting.

choices.text: Start a zonal shift for the affected ALB in ARC, specifying the AZ to evacuate and the expiration time.
choices.explanation: This avoids traffic to that AZ while continuing to use the remaining AZs.

choices.text: Start a Region-wide DNS failover in Route 53.
choices.explanation: This switches a broader scope than required when the remaining AZs in the same Region should continue serving traffic.

source.label: Amazon ARCの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A zonal shift temporarily moves traffic away from one AZ for a supported resource.
learning.concept: Its switching scope differs from Region-wide DNS failover.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Handling Application Initialization Before Demand Increases
prompt: Preparing large dependency data after an EC2 instance starts causes scale-out to take 15 minutes before new capacity becomes available. Daytime load is unpredictable, and you want to prepare initialized instances in advance while using a stopped state. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Enable only detailed monitoring in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This changes the observation interval for demand but does not create prepared capacity.

choices.text: Increase the health check grace period to 15 minutes for every instance.
choices.explanation: This only makes it less likely that an incompletely prepared instance is replaced; it does not change initialization time.

choices.text: Reduce the current desired capacity and create an uninitialized instance each time an increase is requested.
choices.explanation: This cannot provide the prepared capacity needed during a sudden increase.

choices.text: Add a warm pool to the Auto Scaling group and keep instances stopped after initialization.
choices.explanation: During a sudden increase, initialized instances can be started and added to the service.

source.label: Amazon EC2 Auto Scalingの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A warm pool keeps preinitialized instances available in a waiting state.
learning.concept: Part of the initialization process can be skipped during scale-out.

sourceLabel: Official Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling documentation

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Reviewing Which Resources Will Be Replaced by the Next Change
prompt: Before updating an instance managed by CloudFormation, an operator wants to review which resources will be added, modified, or removed when a new template is applied, and whether replacement of existing resources is proposed. What can provide this review without changing the current stack?

choices.text: Create an update change set and inspect the resources' Action and Replacement values.
choices.explanation: After creation, the planned changes can be reviewed without updating the stack.

choices.text: Run drift detection only.
choices.explanation: This checks differences between the current definition and the actual resources; it does not calculate changes from the next template.

choices.text: Create a new stack with the same template under another name and interpret the result as an update to production.
choices.explanation: A new stack creation does not show a replacement plan for existing resources.

choices.text: Use a successful CloudFormation ValidateTemplate result to conclude that no resources will be replaced.
choices.explanation: Template validation differs from comparing changes for a specific stack.

source.label: AWS CloudFormationの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A planned update can be compared with the current declaration to review candidate changes.
learning.concept: A change set applies the normal update only when it is executed.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Complete creation after instances finish initialization
prompt: An Auto Scaling group launched by CloudFormation has initialization processing on all three instances. You do not want the stack creation to be considered successful merely because EC2 instances have started; you want it completed only after confirming that all three instances are ready. Which changes should you make? Select two.

choices.text: Use only the template's DependsOn to detect completion of User Data.
choices.explanation: It controls the creation order of dependencies but does not report successful preparation inside an instance.

choices.text: Set the desired capacity to three and treat that alone as proof that the operations application is ready.
choices.explanation: Specifying the desired number of instances does not confirm that configuration processing succeeded.

choices.text: Send a success notification using cfn-signal after initialization succeeds on each instance.
choices.explanation: This can notify the stack that each instance has finished its preparation.

choices.text: Enable only CloudFormation Termination Protection.
choices.explanation: This protects against deletion and does not affect the creation-completion decision.

choices.text: In the group's CreationPolicy, specify three ResourceSignal signals and a maximum waiting time.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation can use these settings to determine the number of signals required before considering creation complete.

source.label: AWS CloudFormationの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Send readiness signals to CloudFormation and do not mark creation complete until the required number has been received.
learning.concept: The result of configuration processing that runs after infrastructure is created can also be reflected in the stack's completion decision.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Prevent replacement of a critical database during normal stack updates
prompt: An application and a database are in the same CloudFormation stack. Normal application updates and database configuration changes that do not require replacement should be allowed, but Update:Replace for a specific database logical ID should be denied by default. What should you do?

choices.text: Enable only stack termination protection.
choices.explanation: This controls deletion of the entire stack and does not prevent part of a normal update.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain.
choices.explanation: It does not prevent replacement during an update; it retains the old resource after replacement.

choices.text: Remove only the database read permissions from the CloudFormation execution role.
choices.explanation: This cannot be limited to replacement and could also break normal updates and state retrieval.

choices.text: Use a stack policy to deny Update:Replace for the database logical ID while allowing other necessary updates.
choices.explanation: This limits replacement of the specified database during normal stack updates.

source.label: AWS CloudFormationの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A stack policy can specify which actions and resources are permitted during updates.
learning.concept: Distinguish the control that prevents replacement of an existing resource from the control that retains the old resource after replacement.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Complete deletion of an external resource that no longer exists
prompt: A CloudFormation custom resource stores registration information in an internal service. When the stack is deleted, the registration has already been manually removed, so the handler receives a 404 from the deletion API. How should it proceed so that deletion completes safely even when the request is repeated?

choices.text: Respond with success for every external API error.
choices.explanation: This would treat cases such as authorization errors or temporary failures, where deletion was not performed, as completed.

choices.text: Re-create the registration immediately before deletion and always create it again if the request fails.
choices.explanation: This introduces a new side effect during deletion retries and causes unnecessary re-registration.

choices.text: For a 404, send no response and wait for CloudFormation to infer that the target has disappeared.
choices.explanation: A custom resource must send the required response; otherwise the operation can time out while waiting.

choices.text: When a 404 confirms that the target already does not exist, return SUCCESS from the custom resource.
choices.explanation: The desired state has already been reached, so completion can be reported to CloudFormation.

source.label: AWS CloudFormationの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The goal of deletion is to ensure that the target is in a nonexistent state.
learning.concept: Distinguish deletion when the target is absent from cases such as authentication errors where its existence cannot be determined.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Distribute an internal agent as a versioned package
prompt: You need to distribute an internal monitoring agent to Linux managed nodes. For auditing, you must version the installation files together with the installation procedure and install a specific version on each target. The application is not included in the OS vendor's update list. What should you use?

choices.text: Connect to each node with Session Manager and have each administrator copy the latest version from the terminal.
choices.explanation: This depends on manual work and does not establish specified, reproducible versions.

choices.text: Register the package and version with Systems Manager Distributor, then install the specified version on the managed nodes.
choices.explanation: It manages the artifact and procedure together as a package and allows the installed version to be controlled.

choices.text: Wait for the internal application to appear in the OS vendor's updates by using Patch Manager.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a configuration for registering and distributing a custom package at a specified version.

choices.text: Output the agent's file name to CloudWatch Logs and use that to handle installation.
choices.explanation: Recording a file name alone does not distribute or install the application.

source.label: AWS Systems Managerの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The application's package can be managed together with its version and installation procedure.
learning.concept: Distinguish selecting OS patches from distributing an internal application package.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Passing an ID found during inspection to the next step
prompt: An AWS Systems Manager Automation workflow searches for the target EBS volumes and specifies one volume found by the next step as the backup target. The first step can output VolumeId. The target ID is unknown when the execution starts. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Define VolumeId in the first step's Outputs, then reference the step name and output name in the next step's input.
choices.explanation: The ID returned by the search can be passed to the subsequent operation within the same execution.

choices.text: Give both steps the same name so that all evaluated values are shared automatically.
choices.explanation: Using the same name does not reference output values and also creates duplicate step names.

choices.text: Send the search result only to CloudWatch Logs, and use a fixed ID in the next step.
choices.explanation: The target cannot be changed to match the search result.

choices.text: Require the user to enter the volume ID before starting the execution.
choices.explanation: The value is determined by the search, so this does not create a dynamic connection between the steps.

source.label: AWS Systems Managerの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A declared step output can be referenced by a subsequent step.
learning.concept: Input parameters known when an execution starts are distinct from step outputs determined during the execution.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Migrating a shared reference name before deleting it
prompt: Multiple CloudFormation stacks use an Export from the same network stack with Fn::ImportValue. You want to change the export name to follow a new naming convention while keeping the currently consuming stacks running. In what order should you update them?

choices.text: Leave the consuming stack templates unchanged and change only the name of the original export.
choices.explanation: A value in use cannot be switched by changing only its reference name.

choices.text: Add an export with the new name, change all consuming stacks to use the new name, and then delete the old name.
choices.explanation: Each update has a valid reference, and the export in use is not changed prematurely.

choices.text: Delete all consuming stacks and recreate the original export.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement that the stacks continue running.

choices.text: Delete the old export first, then find and update the consuming stacks.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation rejects deletion of an export that is still in use.

source.label: AWS CloudFormationの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The original export cannot be deleted or changed while another stack references it with ImportValue.
learning.concept: Publish the old and new reference names in parallel, switch the consuming stacks, and then delete the old name.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Operating approved product deployments without granting individual permissions
prompt: An operations department distributes reviewed configurations through AWS Service Catalog. Approved users can launch the product, but they are not granted permission to create each AWS resource in the configuration directly. The execution role used to deploy the product is already available. Where should it be associated?

choices.text: Use a template constraint only to validate parameter values.
choices.explanation: Parameter values can be restricted, but this does not configure the IAM role used for deployment.

choices.text: Only give the product the same name as the execution role through its tags.
choices.explanation: Tags do not cause an execution role to be selected.

choices.text: For the target product in the portfolio, configure a launch constraint that uses the available IAM role.
choices.explanation: Deployment can be delegated to the execution role without increasing the users' direct permissions.

choices.text: Grant all users direct permission to perform every AWS API operation used by the product.
choices.explanation: Users could operate outside the approved product, which does not meet the requirement to delegate deployment within the specified scope.

source.label: AWS Service Catalogの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A Service Catalog launch constraint can specify the IAM role used to deploy a product.
learning.concept: Permissions to use a product can be separated from the execution permissions that operate the underlying resources.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Updating while preserving workload eviction constraints
prompt: An update of an EKS managed node group is stopped by PodEvictionFailure. Operations must preserve the PodDisruptionBudget and avoid force-deleting pods when doing so would leave too few available replicas. What should you do?

choices.text: Check the number of replicas and the available placement capacity, make the environment able to satisfy the PDB, and retry the normal update.
choices.explanation: This enables safe pod eviction and a node update that respects the constraint.

choices.text: Assume that pods with the same names will be created automatically on the new nodes and ignore the failure.
choices.explanation: The update failed, so successful replacement has not been confirmed.

choices.text: Remove only the failure indicator from the CloudWatch dashboard.
choices.explanation: This does not make the running pods eligible for eviction.

choices.text: Run the update with force and immediately force-delete pods whose eviction failed.
choices.explanation: A forced method that does not respect the PDB violates the requirement.

source.label: Amazon EKSの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The required spare capacity and pod availability conditions for evicting pods from existing nodes must both be satisfied.
learning.concept: When a normal update cannot evict pods, check the workload placement and running count so that the PDB can be respected.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Apply consistent metadata settings to new EC2 instances at launch
prompt: The operations team creates new EC2 instances from a launch template. Regardless of differences in the settings contained in the AMIs, every instance launched from this template must require IMDSv2 tokens. Which method achieves this without affecting existing instances?

choices.text: Add IMDSv2 to the AMI name only to fix the launch setting.
choices.explanation: The AMI name is not used for metadata options.

choices.text: Set HttpTokens to required in the metadata settings of the launch template version being used.
choices.explanation: This makes IMDSv2 mandatory for new instances launched explicitly from that version.

choices.text: Set only the deployment operator’s IAM session name to IMDSv2.
choices.explanation: The session name is not reflected in the metadata options of created EC2 instances.

choices.text: Deny general HTTP traffic in the network ACLs of all instances.
choices.explanation: This affects user traffic and does not configure IMDS authentication at the template level.

source.label: Amazon EC2の公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Metadata options specified at launch can take precedence.
learning.concept: Changing a launch template setting does not immediately change the options of existing instances.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Specify AMI distribution targets by account and Region
prompt: An Image Builder pipeline can create and test AMIs. Operations wants to distribute the same tested configuration to a different Region in another AWS account. The required distribution permissions and KMS keys are already prepared. Which item should be configured?

choices.text: Set the source Region’s AMI ID in a local EC2 launch template.
choices.explanation: AMI IDs are Region-specific, and this does not distribute an AMI to another Region.

choices.text: Configure the destination Region and target account in a Distribution configuration and use it in the pipeline.
choices.explanation: This specifies the account and Region to which the AMI should be delivered.

choices.text: Change only the Image Builder recipe name to the destination account number.
choices.explanation: A recipe name does not specify a destination account or Region.

choices.text: Only notify an SNS topic that the build succeeded.
choices.explanation: Receiving a notification does not distribute the AMI.

source.label: EC2 Image Builderの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The build and test definition is separate from specifying the account and Region to which the AMI is delivered.
learning.concept: Associate distribution settings with the pipeline to manage where successful images are sent.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Run a process at 9:00 a.m. local time every weekday despite daylight-saving changes
prompt: A process must run at 9:00 a.m. every weekday to match the start of business for a European team. The local time must remain consistent before and after daylight-saving-time changes, and the team does not want to adjust a UTC cron expression manually. Which setting should be used?

choices.text: Set the applicable IANA time zone in the EventBridge Scheduler cron expression.
choices.explanation: The process can run at 9:00 a.m. on local weekdays, including across daylight-saving-time changes.

choices.text: Set a rate expression that runs every 30 days and coincides with the weekday start time.
choices.explanation: A fixed interval does not represent a time on every weekday.

choices.text: Change only the display time zone in CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: Changing the displayed time does not change the scheduler’s execution time.

choices.text: Specify a UTC cron expression that is the same year-round and treat it as the same local time year-round.
choices.explanation: The offset from UTC changes before and after daylight-saving-time changes.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge Schedulerの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An EventBridge Scheduler cron expression can be evaluated using the specified time zone.
learning.concept: Converting a local schedule to a fixed UTC time causes the execution time to shift when daylight-saving time changes.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Monitor standard output while maintenance commands are running
prompt: Run Command is executed on dozens of instances. The first few kilobytes are insufficient for troubleshooting, and the team needs to follow each instance’s standard output and standard error in CloudWatch Logs while execution is in progress. The managed nodes already have the required log permissions. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Open only the EC2 diagnostics screen, treating it as the same as the target instances’ system logs, without any additional configuration.
choices.explanation: This does not configure streams for Run Command standard output and standard error.

choices.text: Use only the initial portion displayed in the console’s Run Command section to obtain the complete output.
choices.explanation: Output beyond the display limit cannot be viewed from that section alone.

choices.text: Send the output to the AWS Config list of noncompliant resources.
choices.explanation: Compliance evaluation results and forwarding command output serve different purposes.

choices.text: Enable output with CloudWatchOutputConfig and specify a log group.
choices.explanation: The output streams for each command and instance can then be viewed in CloudWatch Logs.

source.label: AWS Systems Managerの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The destination for Run Command output can be specified at execution time.
learning.concept: With CloudWatch output, transferred output can be monitored without waiting for the command to finish.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Preview deletion candidates when cleaning up unused images
prompt: An ECR repository contains old untagged images that must be cleaned up. You need to verify whether the new rules will expire any important images before deleting actual images. What should you do?

choices.text: Preview the new policy, then review the expiration candidates before applying it.
choices.explanation: This lets you verify in advance whether unintended images will be selected.

choices.text: Apply the lifecycle policy, then check only the images that were deleted.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to check the candidates before actual deletion.

choices.text: Run an ECR scan and use the number of vulnerabilities as the expiration candidates.
choices.explanation: Security scanning does not evaluate retention periods or tag conditions.

choices.text: Change only the latest-tag string and infer the deletion candidates.
choices.explanation: This does not observe the policy evaluation results for untagged images.

source.label: Amazon ECRの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A lifecycle preview lets you inspect which images a rule targets.
learning.concept: The preview evaluates the targets; automatic deletion begins after the policy is applied.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Include only reads of the target path in the audit
prompt: The audit team wants CloudTrail to record individual GetObject operations for the audit-target prefix in an S3 business bucket. They do not want to expand logging to reads or writes for other prefixes. Which configuration should they use?

choices.text: Monitor only S3 BucketSizeBytes and infer the users who performed reads from the value.
choices.explanation: An aggregated size metric does not include the individual principals that performed reads.

choices.text: Change only the display filter in CloudTrail Event History.
choices.explanation: This does not configure additional data events to be stored.

choices.text: Select S3 object data events and specify the target ARN prefix and GetObject.
choices.explanation: This includes only the target data events in the audit.

choices.text: Specify only ReadOnly as a management event.
choices.explanation: Object GetObject operations are not added as management events.

source.label: AWS CloudTrailの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Configure data events to record individual object operations.
learning.concept: Advanced event selectors can narrow the scope by object ARN and event name.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Delegate role creation while setting a permissions limit
prompt: A development team must be able to create IAM roles for its own workloads. Even if the team attaches broad policies to a new role, you want to ensure that it cannot exceed the range of AWS operations approved by the central team. You will not grant permissions directly to the role through resource-based policies. What should you implement?

choices.text: Standardize the prefix of role names as delegate and allow policies to be unrestricted.
choices.explanation: Naming alone cannot enforce a permissions limit.

choices.text: Set a restriction only on the creator's session and leave new roles unrestricted.
choices.explanation: This does not restrict permissions used later by the separately created role.

choices.text: Require an approved Permissions Boundary when creating a role and prevent the team from removing it.
choices.explanation: The role's permissions can be limited to the range allowed by the boundary and the policies attached by the team.

choices.text: Add tags to each role without adding any authorization controls beyond the tags.
choices.explanation: Tags alone do not reduce the permissions granted by attached action policies.

source.label: AWS IAMの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A permissions boundary limits the maximum range of permissions that can be granted by a role's identity-based policies.
learning.concept: The boundary itself does not grant permissions. The delegating configuration must also prevent the team from removing the boundary.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Allow a recipient role to decrypt shared ciphertext
prompt: A role in account B must decrypt ciphertext encrypted with a customer managed KMS key in account A. Ownership of the key must remain in account A. Permissions to retrieve the data from S3 and other services have already been granted. Which combination is required on the KMS side? Select two.

choices.text: Configure a KMS alias with the same name in B so that it can use the original key for decryption.
choices.explanation: An alias for a different key cannot decrypt data encrypted with A's key.

choices.text: Change only the S3 bucket ACL so that the key can also be used for decryption.
choices.explanation: Data read permissions do not grant KMS decryption permissions.

choices.text: Only extend the key-rotation interval in A.
choices.explanation: Key rotation does not grant the role in B permission to decrypt.

choices.text: In A's key policy, allow decryption by using the target role in B.
choices.explanation: The key owner must authorize operations from the other account.

choices.text: In the IAM policy for B's role, allow kms:Decrypt on A's key.
choices.explanation: The caller must also be granted decryption permission on the target key.

source.label: AWS KMSの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Cross-account KMS use requires permissions on both the key side and the caller side.
learning.concept: Permissions for KMS actions are separate from permissions to read the ciphertext.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Distinguishing the secret immediately before rotation from the current secret
prompt: Secrets Manager automatically rotates database credentials. After an update, an earlier retrieval process is pinned to an old version. How can the application obtain the current value without setting a new version ID on every rotation?

choices.text: Save the latest version ID only once and use it unchanged thereafter.
choices.explanation: This does not follow the move to the new staging label.

choices.text: Call GetSecretValue without fixing VersionId and retrieve the current AWSCURRENT version.
choices.explanation: After rotation completes, the new current version can be retrieved with the same specification.

choices.text: Always retrieve AWSPREVIOUS.
choices.explanation: This refers to the immediately previous version, not the current version.

choices.text: Always retrieve AWSPENDING.
choices.explanation: This refers to a candidate during rotation and is not necessarily the completed current version.

source.label: AWS Secrets Managerの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: During rotation, the AWSCURRENT label moves to the current version.
learning.concept: A fixed version ID does not follow the movement of the staging label.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Recording the operations performed during an audited session
prompt: Administrative work is performed on an EC2 instance with Session Manager. The audit must retain both the session-start record and the operations performed in the corresponding interactive shell. The current procedure tunnels an SSH connection through Session Manager, and specifying a log destination in the session settings does not reveal the contents. What should be changed?

choices.text: Keep the current SSH tunnel and enable only the CloudTrail record for StartSession.
choices.explanation: The API history can be audited, but it does not include operations performed inside SSH.

choices.text: Use the corresponding standard Session Manager shell and configure a destination for session logs.
choices.explanation: The input and output of the session that provides the shell can be recorded in the designated log store.

choices.text: Change the SSH port and assume that the tunnel data becomes plaintext.
choices.explanation: Changing the port does not change whether the communication is encrypted or recordable.

choices.text: Shorten the maximum session duration so that the contents are saved automatically.
choices.explanation: Session duration does not change what type of logs are available.

source.label: AWS Systems Managerの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Whether contents can be recorded depends on the type of Session Manager session.
learning.concept: SSH and port forwarding tunnel encrypted data, so their contents cannot be recorded.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Requiring TLS while preserving service delivery
prompt: Explicitly deny non-TLS client access to S3. Existing delivery by an AWS service principal is allowed by a separate permission, and the delivery must not be denied because network condition keys are absent from service-to-service calls. How should the deny condition be designed?

choices.text: Put the TLS condition in the CloudFront cache policy and do not apply it to S3.
choices.explanation: This does not explicitly deny direct access to S3.

choices.text: Remove the TLS condition and rely only on S3 server-side encryption.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest does not require TLS on the network connection.

choices.text: Include service principals in the non-TLS deny and place the service Allow statement later.
choices.explanation: An explicit deny takes precedence over Allow statements; statement order cannot override it.

choices.text: Explicitly deny the request when aws:SecureTransport is false and aws:PrincipalIsAWSService is also false.
choices.explanation: This denies non-TLS client access while preserving the separate permission for the service principal.

source.label: Amazon S3の公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Network-derived condition keys may be missing from service-to-service requests.
learning.concept: A condition that excludes approved service calls can coexist with requiring TLS for direct access.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Verifying that stored audit files were not altered
prompt: You want to verify whether CloudTrail files stored in S3 were altered or deleted after delivery. Starting with future deliveries, you want to use the verification files delivered by AWS. What should you configure?

choices.text: Enable trail log file integrity validation and compare the digest with the logs during verification.
choices.explanation: Signed digests can be used to verify tampering and missing logs that were expected to be delivered.

choices.text: Check only the S3 object's LastModified value and use it to guarantee whether changes occurred.
choices.explanation: A timestamp alone cannot guarantee the contents of the log or the absence of files that should have been delivered.

choices.text: Only enable log encryption and consider every decryptable file to be unmodified.
choices.explanation: This does not compare the file with a separately re-encrypted legitimate file.

choices.text: Record only the number of CloudTrail logs reported by CloudWatch each day.
choices.explanation: A count cannot inspect a specific file or its signature.

source.label: AWS CloudTrailの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: CloudTrail can deliver digest files containing log hashes and signatures.
learning.concept: Separate the configuration that generates integrity evidence from the operation that actually validates files for the target period.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Observe the impact of new blocking rules first
prompt: A managed rule group is being added to an existing AWS WAF web ACL. The existing rules must remain enabled, while all rules in the new group must be prevented from blocking production traffic so that matches can be monitored before enforcement. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Set a Count override for each rule in the new group and review the logs or metrics for matches.
choices.explanation: The new rules continue to evaluate requests, allowing their impact to be observed before they block traffic.

choices.text: Set the action for every rule to Block and estimate the impact from the number of inquiries received from production users.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement not to block production requests during evaluation.

choices.text: Place a rule with the highest priority that allows all requests before the new group is invoked.
choices.explanation: Neither the subsequent new rules nor the existing protection rules will be evaluated.

choices.text: Detach the web ACL from the production application and use metrics from the unassociated group as the number of incidents.
choices.explanation: Production traffic is not evaluated, and the existing protections are also removed.

source.label: AWS WAFの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The actions of the rules in the target group can be overridden to Count for validation.
learning.concept: This allows the new rules to be observed without changing the web ACL's default behavior or the scope of existing allow rules.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Scan uploads and pass the results to downstream processing
prompt: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 scans objects uploaded to a selected prefix. Downstream processing must check the object tags set by GuardDuty. Which settings are required for tagging? Select two.

choices.text: Enable result tagging in the scan plan.
choices.explanation: This configures the service to apply tags corresponding to the scan results.

choices.text: Grant only IAM permissions for CloudWatch Logs and deny writes to S3 tags.
choices.explanation: The service will not be able to apply tags.

choices.text: Grant the GuardDuty service role permission to tag the target objects.
choices.explanation: This supplies the permission required to write scan results to the protected objects.

choices.text: Use only bucket versioning and consider all older versions safe.
choices.explanation: The existence of object versions does not record scan results.

choices.text: Manually set every object tag to safe.
choices.explanation: The actual scan results will not be passed to downstream processing.

source.label: Amazon GuardDutyの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Consider separately enabling scanning and configuring the results to be retained as object tags.
learning.concept: When tags are used, the service role must have the permissions required to tag the target objects.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Retain the DNS validation record used for automatic renewal
prompt: A public certificate validated with DNS in ACM is associated with an ALB. The initial issuance is complete, and the DNS administrator is about to delete the validation CNAME. What should be done to use ACM automatic renewal without interrupting the service?

choices.text: Shorten only the DNS record's TTL and delete the validation CNAME.
choices.explanation: A shorter TTL cannot replace a validation record that no longer exists.

choices.text: Export the certificate issuance time from CloudTrail and use it instead of DNS during renewal.
choices.explanation: Issuance history does not validate control of the domain.

choices.text: Delete the CNAME, detach the certificate from the ALB, and wait for renewal.
choices.explanation: This removes both the validation record and the certificate's in-use status, so the automatic-renewal requirements are not met.

choices.text: Keep the validation CNAME in public DNS and keep the certificate in use on the target ALB.
choices.explanation: ACM can then verify the validation and in-use status required for renewal.

source.label: AWS Certificate Managerの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Automatic renewal for DNS validation requires ACM to verify both the validation CNAME and the certificate's in-use status.
learning.concept: The validation record continues to be used after issuance.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Investigate the location of sensitive data in specified buckets
prompt: For an audit, sensitive data that may contain personally identifiable information must be identified in CSV files and other data stored in several S3 buckets. Which service can provide inspection results for a specified scope without requiring the operations team to download all the contents?

choices.text: Search for personal information in object contents using only S3 management events in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: Management API history does not include object contents.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to inspect external sharing and treat anything found as personal information.
choices.explanation: It can analyze sharing permissions, but it cannot determine the data type in the object contents.

choices.text: Change the S3 storage class and infer sensitive information from the storage cost.
choices.explanation: Storage cost and class do not classify the meaning of a file.

choices.text: Create a sensitive data discovery job in Macie for the target buckets and select the required data identifiers.
choices.explanation: Macie can analyze the target content and produce sensitive-data discovery results.

source.label: Amazon Macieの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A Macie sensitive data discovery job can specify target S3 buckets and analyze their data.
learning.concept: Distinguish inspection of configuration exposure from sensitive-data discovery in object contents.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Continuously Collecting Rejected-Connection 5-Tuples
prompt: A team needs to retain which connections were rejected on multiple ENIs in a VPC and analyze them by time period using source and destination addresses, ports, and protocols. Packet contents are not needed, and no additional network appliances can be deployed. What should the team enable?

choices.text: Store only EC2 start and stop operations from CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This does not include metadata for individual connections that traversed the network.

choices.text: Copy the DNS zone file and infer the ports of rejected traffic.
choices.explanation: Records do not reveal whether connections actually occurred or were rejected.

choices.text: Store only the results from Reachability Analyzer and use them as the number of connections that occurred.
choices.explanation: This service analyzes paths from configuration and does not record every flow that actually occurred.

choices.text: Create VPC Flow Logs for rejected traffic on the target ENIs or subnets and send them to an analysis destination.
choices.explanation: The logs can record the source and destination of rejected flows, ports, and other metadata.

source.label: Amazon VPCの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: VPC Flow Logs continuously collect communication metadata.
learning.concept: Distinguish configuration-based reachability simulation from flows that were actually observed.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Why Only a Specific Destination Uses a Different Route
prompt: A VPC subnet route table has a route that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT gateway and a route that sends 10.42.16.0/24 to a Transit Gateway. An administrator expected a packet destined for 10.42.16.35 to go to the NAT gateway. When both routes are active, which route is used?

choices.text: Send the packet to the NAT gateway because the default route always has priority.
choices.explanation: The name and value 0.0.0.0 do not override the longest-prefix-match rule.

choices.text: Use whichever route was added more recently.
choices.explanation: Creation order does not take precedence over prefix length.

choices.text: Duplicate the packet to both destinations and select the route that responds first.
choices.explanation: A VPC route table does not duplicate the same packet to both matching routes.

choices.text: Send the packet to the Transit Gateway because it matches 10.42.16.0/24.
choices.explanation: The /24 route is more specific than the /0 route and therefore takes priority.

source.label: Amazon VPCの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The longest prefix is selected when multiple routes match.
learning.concept: A default route applies when no more specific route exists for the destination.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Inventorying Address Usage Across Accounts Before Connecting Networks
prompt: The number of manually allocated VPCs has grown across multiple accounts in Organizations. Before integrating the networks, the team wants to centrally inventory the CIDRs of VPCs in approved Regions and continuously identify overlaps and existing allocations that are outside management. Which approach does this without changing routes yet?

choices.text: Connect the VPCs to the same Transit Gateway first and use only the propagated routes to identify allocations.
choices.explanation: This changes connectivity first and cannot fully inventory overlapping CIDRs from the routes.

choices.text: Add up the NAT Gateway connection counts in CloudWatch to calculate CIDR overlaps.
choices.explanation: Connection counts do not contain each VPC's allocated CIDR or its overlap status.

choices.text: Integrate the advanced tier of VPC IPAM with the organization and use the same private scope to inspect CIDR usage and overlaps in the target Regions.
choices.explanation: This does not change routes and can provide address information detected across multiple accounts.

choices.text: Review only recent VPC creation events in CloudTrail and exclude VPCs created before that period from the inventory.
choices.explanation: Creation history for only a limited period cannot cover existing allocations or current state.

source.label: Amazon VPCの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Within the scope monitored by VPC IPAM, existing VPC CIDR usage and overlaps can be reviewed per resource.
learning.concept: CIDR inventory and configuring new network routes can proceed as separate steps.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Why an Existing Parent-Zone Record Cannot Be Resolved Through an Empty Child Zone
prompt: The same VPC has private hosted zones for example.internal and team.example.internal. The parent zone contains a record for api.team.example.internal, but the child zone has no record with the same name and type. There is no conflicting Resolver forwarding rule. What happens when the name is queried from the VPC, and where should it be fixed?

choices.text: The child zone is selected and NXDOMAIN is returned, so create the required record in the child zone according to the management policy.
choices.explanation: Resolution can be enabled by placing the data in the zone that handles the query.

choices.text: Set the TTL of the same record in the parent zone to 0; this changes which child zone is selected.
choices.explanation: TTL does not affect selection based on zone-name specificity.

choices.text: A name missing from the child zone is always searched again in the parent zone, so no change is required.
choices.explanation: The result from the most specific zone is not automatically queried again in the parent zone.

choices.text: Re-create the private hosted zone for example.internal as a public hosted zone.
choices.explanation: This does not change selection of the specific child zone and would expose private names publicly.

source.label: Amazon Route 53の公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: For overlapping private hosted zones associated with the same VPC, the most specific zone is selected.
learning.concept: If the selected zone lacks the record, Route 53 does not return to the parent zone to query it again.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Allow reads only through CloudFront while keeping S3 private
prompt: The CloudFront origin is a standard S3 REST endpoint. Keep static files retrievable from CloudFront while making the bucket private. Which combination of settings should be used? Select two.

choices.text: Configure an OAC that signs requests to the CloudFront S3 origin.
choices.explanation: This authenticates origin requests from CloudFront.

choices.text: Configure only the behavior setting that redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
choices.explanation: This controls communication between viewers and the edge, but does not change permission for direct reads from S3.

choices.text: Allow s3:GetObject from the target distribution in the bucket policy, and do not allow anonymous access.
choices.explanation: This limits origin reads to the target distribution.

choices.text: Prevent direct access simply by assigning the S3 bucket name a private alias in DNS.
choices.explanation: An alias for the route does not change the bucket's authorization.

choices.text: Use the S3 website endpoint and sign requests to that endpoint with OAC.
choices.explanation: The website endpoint cannot use OAC as a standard S3 origin.

source.label: Amazon CloudFrontの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Use CloudFront OAC to sign origin requests and restrict delivery with the S3 bucket policy.
learning.concept: Viewer access and the callers permitted by the origin bucket can be controlled separately.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Forward only the audit header to the origin
prompt: CloudFront serves the same image. You want to log the X-Device-Class sent by the client only for requests that actually reach the origin. The image is identical regardless of the value, and you do not want to split the cache key. Where should this be configured?

choices.text: Add the header to the origin request policy and do not include it in the cache policy key.
choices.explanation: This adds the value to origin requests while preserving the existing cache granularity.

choices.text: Set a fixed value with the same name in the origin custom headers.
choices.explanation: This cannot record the actual value for each viewer.

choices.text: Add a header with the same name to the CloudFront response headers policy.
choices.explanation: This configures the response returned to viewers and does not forward the header in origin requests.

choices.text: Add the header only to the cache policy key.
choices.explanation: Requests with different values will be placed in separate cache entries.

source.label: Amazon CloudFrontの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An origin request policy can forward a value that is outside the cache key.
learning.concept: Also consider that a cache hit does not generate an origin request.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Delegate a child zone from the parent domain to a separate team
prompt: One team manages the parent domain example.com. Another team should manage the public hosted zone public.eu.example.com that it created in Route 53. The child-zone records are already configured, but general resolvers cannot find the child from the parent. What should be configured on the parent side?

choices.text: Create only a TXT record for the child-zone name in the parent zone.
choices.explanation: A TXT record does not delegate the child zone.

choices.text: Create an NS record for the child-zone name in the parent zone and register the name servers assigned to the child's hosted zone.
choices.explanation: Recursive resolvers can discover the child zone from the parent's response.

choices.text: Delete the child zone's SOA record and use the parent zone's SOA record unchanged.
choices.explanation: The parent's existing SOA record does not create delegation for the child's name resolution.

choices.text: Change all of the parent's NS records to point to the child zone, moving resolution for the entire parent zone to the child.
choices.explanation: Only the child name needs to be delegated; the entire parent zone should not be affected.

source.label: Amazon Route 53の公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Specify the child zone's authoritative name servers with an NS record in the parent zone.
learning.concept: This separates administrative authority between the parent and child, allowing the child team to manage records within the child zone.

title: Pass TLS through to the application without terminating it at the load balancer
prompt: The networking team receives TCP 443 traffic with an NLB. Certificate management and TLS termination must continue at each existing target's application, and the NLB must forward the encrypted bytes without modifying them. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Add an HTTP listener and path conditions to the NLB, and select the encrypted requests based on their contents.
choices.explanation: This is not a configuration in which the NLB forwards traffic based on HTTP paths.

choices.text: Forward from a TCP 443 listener to a TCP target group, and terminate TLS at the targets.
choices.explanation: The original TLS traffic can be delivered over TCP without decryption at the listener.

choices.text: Add a certificate to an NLB TLS listener and have it forward only a raw TLS stream without decryption.
choices.explanation: A TLS listener terminates the client TLS connection at the NLB.

choices.text: Open only TCP 80 and assume that existing clients configured for 443 can connect through the same path without changes.
choices.explanation: This does not accept the port 443 specified by the clients.

source.label: Elastic Load Balancingの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: When an NLB uses a TLS listener, the load balancer terminates the connection.
learning.concept: To pass TLS through to the targets, send the traffic to them through a TCP listener.

title: Prepare for an AWS-side VPN tunnel outage with a dedicated VPN
prompt: An on-premises device supports BGP and currently uses only one of the two tunnels provided by AWS Site-to-Site VPN. You want communication to continue when the AWS-side tunnel is updated. What should you do without adding another device?

choices.text: Save a second configuration for backup, but do not create the connection.
choices.explanation: A functioning tunnel is required to switch traffic away from the path under maintenance.

choices.text: Increase the MTU of the normally used tunnel to provide redundancy.
choices.explanation: Frame size does not increase the number of paths or provide failover.

choices.text: Configure both tunnels on the device and exchange reachable routes using BGP.
choices.explanation: The remaining route can be used when one tunnel is unavailable.

choices.text: Configure the second tunnel with the same AWS-side IP as the existing tunnel and duplicate the same route.
choices.explanation: This does not configure the route for the separate tunnel provided by AWS.

source.label: AWS Site-to-Site VPNの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A single VPN connection provides two redundant tunnels.
learning.concept: Because either tunnel may be affected by maintenance, configure both tunnels and provide routes through both.

title: Specify the geographic availability of content by country

choices.explanation: Storage settings do not restrict viewers based on their country.

choices.text: Use the CloudFront Price Class to select only edge locations in North America.
choices.explanation: This controls edge locations and pricing; it does not deny users from countries outside the specified area.

choices.text: Set Canada and the United States in the distribution's geographic restriction allowlist.
choices.explanation: The distribution can restrict delivery-side access from countries outside the allowlist.

choices.text: Use only Route 53 latency-based routing.
choices.explanation: Selecting a destination does not deny country-based access to CloudFront.

learning.concept: Access can be evaluated based on the requester's country instead of being implemented separately in each origin application.

title: Restrict the application entry point for a dynamically scaled ALB
prompt: An ALB targets EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group, and the application listens on TCP 8080. You want to prevent direct connections from other EC2 instances in the same VPC and avoid updating rules whenever the load balancer's IP addresses change. What should you configure in the target's security group?

choices.text: In the target's inbound rule for TCP 8080, specify the ALB's security group as the source.
choices.explanation: This allows only the intended traffic without updating individual ALB IP addresses.

choices.text: Hard-code the ALB's current IP addresses in the target rules.
choices.explanation: The rules would need to be updated whenever the ALB IP addresses change.

choices.text: Create no inbound rule for the application in the target's security group.
choices.explanation: Connections initiated by the ALB would also be unable to reach the application.

choices.text: Allow TCP 8080 from the CIDR block of the entire VPC.
choices.explanation: This would also allow direct connections from clients other than the ALB within the VPC.

title: Investigate the history of DNS query names in a VPC

choices.text: Enable query logging dedicated to a public hosted zone and assume that it will also capture all VPC queries.
choices.explanation: Queries to a public hosted zone and records of Resolver use within a VPC are different logging scopes.

choices.explanation: Flow Logs do not retain packet contents.

choices.text: Set the alarm's EvaluationPeriods to 10.
choices.explanation: This specifies the number of data points to evaluate; it does not make the observation interval 10 seconds.

choices.text: Set StorageResolution to 1 when publishing the status, and set the alarm's Period to 10 seconds.
choices.explanation: Data published at high resolution can be used for a 10-second evaluation.

choices.text: Change the dashboard's automatic refresh interval to 10 seconds.
choices.explanation: The screen refresh frequency does not change the metric's resolution.

choices.explanation: Values are not published with the resolution required for a 10-second period.

title: Monitoring a failure rate independent of request volume
prompt: The number of requests to a service varies by time of day. In CloudWatch, you monitor the failure rate for each five-minute period using Errors and Invocations. Both metrics use the same set of dimensions, and the failure rate should not be evaluated during periods with no requests. Which combination should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Compare the Sum of Errors with a fixed value and ignore the request count.
choices.explanation: The error count changes with the load even when the failure rate is the same.

choices.text: Use the value obtained by subtracting Invocations from Errors as the failure rate.
choices.explanation: The result is a difference in counts, not a percentage.

choices.text: Alarm only on the maximum Invocations value for each period.
choices.explanation: This shows the request volume but not the proportion of failed requests.

choices.text: Use the Sum for the same five-minute period for both Errors and Invocations.
choices.explanation: This allows the error count and invocation count for the same interval to be compared.

choices.text: Use a metric math expression that divides Errors by Invocations and multiplies by 100 only when Invocations is positive.
choices.explanation: This excludes periods with no requests while allowing percentage comparisons for periods with requests.

source.label: Amazon CloudWatchの公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Compare the number of failures by dividing the failure count by the request count for the same period.
learning.concept: A conditional calculation can explicitly define the behavior when the denominator is 0.

title: Protecting newly arriving identifiers in an existing log flow
prompt: A new event containing a sensitive identifier arrives in CloudWatch Logs. The application cannot be modified immediately. Standard operators must see the value masked, and an audit record of the detection must be sent to a separate destination. Which settings are appropriate? Select two.

choices.text: Specify an audit destination that records detections in the same policy.
choices.explanation: Detection results can be sent to the selected audit destination.

choices.text: Only encrypt the log group and assume that individual values will also be hidden when viewed.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest does not provide partial masking of values when they are retrieved.

choices.text: Only shorten the retention period.
choices.explanation: Values in logs that remain available are not masked when viewed.

choices.text: Grant logs:Unmask to all operators.
choices.explanation: This allows the masks to be removed and defeats the display restriction for standard operators.

choices.text: Configure the required data identifiers and masking in the data protection policy for the target log group.
choices.explanation: Matching data ingested into the log group can be masked in the default view.

title: Validating evidence before acting on an incident conclusion
prompt: After AWS DevOps Agent completed an incident investigation, it reported that the immediately preceding deployment was the cause. Before approving a rollback, the operations team wants to use a structured evaluation within the product to verify whether the evidence collected by the investigation supports the conclusion. Which feature should they use?

choices.text: Create a rollback procedure as a DevOps task and judge the investigation's quality from the execution result.
choices.explanation: This executes a response step; it does not evaluate whether an existing investigation is supported before approval.

choices.text: Count the number of events in the same investigation timeline and judge the conclusion's certainty from the count alone.
choices.explanation: The timeline can support an investigation, but the count does not evaluate whether individual pieces of evidence support the conclusion.

choices.text: Start another investigation for the same incident and check only whether the names of both possible causes match.
choices.explanation: Matching names alone does not show whether the evidence collected by the existing investigation explains the cause.

choices.text: Run Review on the completed investigation and inspect the Evidence grounding result.
choices.explanation: This evaluates whether the collected evidence supports the conclusion based on the investigation record.

source.label: AWS DevOps Agentの調査レビュー

learning.reason: To verify investigation quality and evidentiary support, run Review on the completed investigation.
learning.concept: Automatic generation of possible causes, evidence evaluation, and approval of response actions are separate decisions.

title: Investigating Shared-Storage Performance Limits from Two Perspectives
prompt: An application’s file operations are slow when using the EFS General Purpose performance mode. The team wants to separately investigate whether it is close to the I/O limit for General Purpose mode and whether its actual throughput is close to the permitted amount. Which combination of metrics should they use? Select two.

choices.text: Look only at StorageBytes and use it as the limit for file-operation counts.
choices.explanation: It measures storage usage, not the requested performance itself.

choices.text: Divide the Sum of MeteredIOBytes by the number of seconds in the period and compare it with PermittedThroughput for the same period.
choices.explanation: This compares the effective measured throughput with the permitted capacity.

choices.text: Check PercentIOLimit.
choices.explanation: It shows the percentage relative to the I/O limit for General Purpose mode.

choices.text: Estimate the active I/O limit from the EFS file system ID.
choices.explanation: The ID does not contain load trends.

choices.text: Calculate the operation ratio using only ClientConnections.
choices.explanation: The number of clients does not reveal the type or amount of I/O consumed.
