In addition to the original event, you want to receive the invocation context and the function's failure information in a single record. What should you configure?

choices.text: Use only a target DLQ on the EventBridge rule to collect the processing result from inside Lambda.
choices.explanation: This handles delivery failures to the target, but not the final execution result after the function has accepted the event.

choices.text: Register SQS as an OnSuccess destination.
choices.explanation: This is for successful results and does not pass along a final failure.

choices.text: Configure the same SQS queue only as the Lambda DLQ.
choices.explanation: This provides an event-centered notification and does not provide the complete invocation record for the failed destination.

choices.text: In the function's asynchronous configuration, register SQS as the OnFailure destination and grant permission to send to it.
choices.explanation: This lets you receive the invocation record for a failure after the configured retries.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: When a failure destination is specified for an asynchronous invocation, Lambda can send an invocation record that includes the execution result.
learning.concept: Distinguish cases where passing along the original event is sufficient from cases that also require the result context.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Separate the units that preserve processing order
prompt: Record updates must preserve arrival order only within the same customer. Events for different customers can be processed in parallel, and you want to add workers as throughput requires. How should you combine the SQS configuration and the identifiers used by the sender? Choose two.

choices.text: Use a random MessageGroupId for each message.
choices.explanation: Messages from the same customer would be placed in different groups, so their order would not be guaranteed.

choices.text: Use an SQS FIFO queue.
choices.explanation: This queue type supports ordering within a group.

choices.text: Share a customer-ID-based MessageGroupId among messages from the same customer.
choices.explanation: Customers can be processed in parallel because they belong to different groups.

choices.text: Set only each customer's MessageDeduplicationId to a fixed value.
choices.explanation: The deduplication ID does not define an ordering group and could cause different updates to be treated as duplicates.

choices.text: Use the same fixed MessageGroupId for all customers.
choices.explanation: All customers would be in one ordering group, so the required parallelism would not be achieved.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An FIFO queue preserves order within the same MessageGroupId and can process different groups concurrently.
learning.concept: When the key is the scope in which order is required, unrelated customers do not have to share the same ordering wait.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Reliably hide items past their expiration time
prompt: You enabled TTL in DynamoDB and use it to automatically delete session items. An item can temporarily appear in read results even after its expiration time has passed. While leaving physical deletion to TTL, how can you prevent expired items from appearing in the application's list during that interval?

choices.text: Align the backup retention period with the session expiration.
choices.explanation: The backup retention period does not change the application's current query results.

choices.text: In the list's Query, compare the current time with the TTL attribute and exclude expired items.
choices.explanation: This applies logical expiration without waiting for asynchronous deletion.

choices.text: Only enable strongly consistent reads.
choices.explanation: Increasing read consistency does not hide items that still exist based on their TTL expiration.

choices.text: Save the TTL attribute again in milliseconds and continue reading.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB TTL attributes must represent Unix time in seconds; changing them to milliseconds does not resolve the problem.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Deletion after a TTL expiration is asynchronous, so an item can remain readable until it is deleted.
learning.concept: Evaluating expiration at access time separates logical expiration from the timing of physical deletion.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Clone a production database quickly using shared storage
prompt: You want to practice recovery procedures with a compatible Aurora cluster. You need to test updates on a separate cluster without writing to the original database. Which feature avoids copying all the original data in advance and consumes capacity as pages change?

choices.text: Perform a backtrack on the production cluster and return to the original session after testing.
choices.explanation: This changes the state of the production cluster and violates the isolation requirement.

choices.text: Clone the Aurora cluster and run the tests against the clone.
choices.explanation: This creates a separate writable cluster by using copy-on-write.

choices.text: Copy the snapshot to another Region and then open a cluster identical to production.
choices.explanation: Copying across Regions is not a procedure that uses the same data pages through copy-on-write.

choices.text: Add a read replica to the original cluster and perform independent writes there.
choices.explanation: A reader in the same Aurora cluster is not an independent write environment.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An Aurora clone uses copy-on-write, so it can initially reference the same storage pages as the source until data changes.
learning.concept: This separates writes made by a test cluster while avoiding an operation that duplicates all data at the start.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Choose a point in time from automated backups in another Region
prompt: You operate the corresponding RDS DB instance in a single Region. During a large-scale failure, you will recover in another Region, but you do not want to run a standby DB during normal operations. You want to replicate transaction logs as well as automated snapshots and choose a point within the available recovery range. What should you do?

choices.text: Run only regular cross-Region copies of manual snapshots.
choices.explanation: This does not automatically provide the logs between snapshots.

choices.text: Use a Multi-AZ standby instance in the same Region.
choices.explanation: This does not provide backups in the specified other Region or point-in-time recovery there.

choices.text: Keep a cross-Region read replica running continuously.
choices.explanation: This violates the constraint against running a standby DB during normal operations and does not provide point-in-time recovery using the logs.

choices.text: Configure RDS cross-Region automated backup replication and check the recoverable times in the destination.
choices.explanation: This avoids running a standby DB and lets you choose a time within the replicated recovery range.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: RDS cross-Region automated backup replication can replicate automated snapshots and transaction logs to the destination.
learning.concept: This provides a different recovery granularity from a procedure that uses only the times represented by copied manual snapshots.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Restore application-specific write locations on shared storage
prompt: You need to restore two application directories on EFS, and each application must remount its designated path. Because client UID settings differ between environments, you want to fix each application's root directory and POSIX ID on the server side. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Provide the same NFS mount to both applications and assign IDs from file-system tags.
choices.explanation: Tags alone do not fix the root directory or POSIX ID.

choices.text: Switch the POSIX user for each application path through the EFS lifecycle.
choices.explanation: The lifecycle feature changes storage classes; it does not affect the ID used during access.

choices.text: Create separate mount targets in each AZ and specify the POSIX ID there.
choices.explanation: A mount target is a connection point in a VPC and does not specify an application-specific POSIX ID.

choices.text: Mount each application through its dedicated EFS access point, specifying the root directory and POSIX user.
choices.explanation: This applies the specified root and ID regardless of differences in the clients' execution environments.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An EFS access point can configure the root visible to the client and the POSIX ID used for access.
learning.concept: It lets you provide a separate mount entry point for each application while keeping the same EFS file system.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Prevent both Regions from being disabled by a failover operation
prompt: Traffic to two Regions is controlled through routing controls in Amazon Application Recovery Controller. Capacity is sufficient, and the procedure may temporarily turn both controls on, but you want to prevent operator error from turning both controls off in advance. What should you configure?

choices.text: For the two controls, configure an assertion rule requiring at least one control to be On.
choices.explanation: This blocks an update that turns both controls off while allowing both controls to be On.

choices.text: Only set the initial value of each routing control to On.
choices.explanation: This does not add a constraint that rejects subsequent operations turning both controls off.

choices.text: Configure only a notification after both controls have been turned off.
choices.explanation: Detecting the result does not prevent the transition to the disabled state.

choices.text: Configure a condition requiring exactly one control to be On at all times.
choices.explanation: This would also reject operating with both controls temporarily On.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An ARC assertion rule can validate a state that a set of routing controls must maintain.
learning.concept: Unlike a runbook or an after-the-fact notification, it rejects an operation that would create a disallowed control state.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Preventing Concentrated Retries During Temporary Failures
prompt: Many Step Functions workflows use the same external business API. Retry transient throttling reported by a Lambda task, but do not retry invalid input. Prevent retries from occurring at the same moment, and limit the number of attempts. What should be configured?

choices.text: Use Catch to replace transient errors with successful completion.
choices.explanation: This treats work that was not performed as successful without retrying the required processing.

choices.text: Configure a Retrier that matches only transient errors, specifying backoff, FULL jitter, and a finite maximum number of attempts.
choices.explanation: This limits the errors that are retried and spreads the retry timing.

choices.text: Only increase the timeout for every Task.
choices.explanation: Increasing the time allowed before completion does not specify which failures to retry or the retry interval.

choices.text: Retry States.ALL with a fixed interval and the same number of attempts.
choices.explanation: This also retries invalid input and does not spread executions that fail at the same time.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A Task Retry can configure the target errors, number of attempts, backoff, and jitter, including NotifyWhenUploaded.
learning.concept: Limiting the reasons for retries helps suppress repeated failures and synchronized load amplification.

category: 信頼性と事業継続
examDomain: 信頼性と事業継続
title: Confirming That Writes Have Reached the Cloud
prompt: You operate a nightly batch that writes to S3 File Gateway through NFS. A downstream job should start after files saved to the shared location have been uploaded to S3. Which mechanism distinguishes that point from the time the files are written to the cache?

choices.text: Request NotifyWhenUploaded after writing to the shared location, and start the downstream job when the corresponding completion notification arrives.
choices.explanation: This links the requested notification to completion of the actual upload.

choices.text: Increase the NFS share's cache capacity and then wait for a fixed period.
choices.explanation: Capacity and a fixed wait do not indicate completion of the transfer for a specific batch.

choices.text: Treat completion of RefreshCache as completion of the upload to S3.
choices.explanation: This updates metadata to reflect changes from S3 in the share; it does not indicate that an upload has finished.

choices.text: Run the downstream process as soon as the client closes the NFS file.
choices.explanation: Closing the file does not guarantee that the asynchronous transfer to S3 is complete.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: S3 File Gateway's NotifyWhenUploaded can confirm that uploads up to the time of the notification request have completed.
learning.concept: A successful local write does not mean that synchronization to S3 has completed.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Moving Existing Resources to Another Stack
prompt: You are reorganizing two CloudFormation stacks in the same Region by responsibility. The resources involved support stack refactoring, and their properties and physical resource IDs must be preserved. Do not include unrelated configuration changes in the same operation. What should you use?

choices.text: First add equivalent resources normally to the destination stack, then delete the resources from the source stack.
choices.explanation: Even with equivalent settings, this creates a second set of physical resources.

choices.text: Create a stack refactoring plan using the source and destination templates, verify the mappings, and execute it.
choices.explanation: This maps the resources being moved and preserves the existing physical resources.

choices.text: Only change the source resource's logical ID through a normal template update.
choices.explanation: This does not transfer management to another stack and may cause the resource to be deleted and recreated during the update.

choices.text: Only reference the stack outputs from the destination stack.
choices.explanation: The source stack remains the resource's managing stack.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Stack refactoring reorganizes stack ownership and logical IDs for existing resources without recreating the resources.
learning.concept: This differs from removing resources from one template and adding them to another through a normal template update.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Protecting a Shared Stack from Deletion
prompt: A CloudFormation root stack contains multiple nested stacks. Approved template updates must continue, but if someone mistakenly calls DeleteStack on the root, the request itself must be rejected. What should be configured?

choices.text: Configure termination protection directly on one nested stack.
choices.explanation: Termination protection for nested stacks is configured from the root stack.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy Retain on one resource in the root stack.
choices.explanation: This does not stop deletion of the stack itself.

choices.text: Use a stack policy to deny Update:Replace for one resource.
choices.explanation: This applies during stack updates and does not stop the specified deletion request.

choices.text: Enable termination protection on the root stack.
choices.explanation: This rejects deletion requests for the root and extends protection to the nested stacks.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Termination protection prevents a direct deletion request for a protected stack.
learning.concept: This applies to a different operation from protecting resources during updates or retaining individual resources after deletion.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Representing a Set of Regular Resource Names in a Template
prompt: You are defining multiple monitoring resources with the same conditions in a CloudFormation template. You want to expand the definition one item at a time from a list of target names while continuing to use the console or CLI through CloudFormation. Which two features should you combine in the template? Select two.

choices.text: Use only Fn::If conditions to iteratively expand a list of arbitrary length.
choices.explanation: Conditions select among existing branches; they do not repeatedly generate resources from a list.

choices.text: Declare the AWS::LanguageExtensions transform in the template.
choices.explanation: This enables the built-in function Fn::ForEach in the template.

choices.text: Specify a list of names and a resource fragment with Fn::ForEach.
choices.explanation: The target resource definition can be expanded for each name.

choices.text: Specify AWS::Include alone to automatically generate any number of monitoring resources.
choices.explanation: This transform loads fragments; it does not define expansion based on the number of records.

choices.text: Use only Fn::Sub to create one resource for each list element.
choices.explanation: String substitution does not duplicate resource declarations.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Fn::ForEach is a built-in function available through LanguageExtensions that expands a template fragment from a collection.
learning.concept: Distinguish selecting a condition or substituting an attribute value from iterating resource declarations.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Registering On-Premises Servers for Operational Commands
prompt: A small number of on-premises Linux servers must be maintained with the same Systems Manager used for AWS EC2. The on-premises servers do not have EC2 instance profiles, but the required outbound communication is possible. Which registration procedure should you use?

choices.text: Only turn on Default Host Management Configuration for EC2.
choices.explanation: This does not perform the procedure for registering the on-premises servers with SSM Agent.

choices.text: Add the on-premises servers to the Systems Manager Inventory and omit the agent.
choices.explanation: Adding inventory information alone does not make the servers nodes on which commands can be run.

choices.text: Create a hybrid activation, install SSM Agent on the targets, and register them with the activation ID and code.
choices.explanation: The servers can be managed as managed nodes without relying on an EC2 instance profile.

choices.text: Give the on-premises server names the same values as EC2 Name tags.
choices.explanation: EC2 tags or names do not register on-premises servers.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A hybrid activation can register external hosts as Systems Manager managed nodes.
learning.concept: Prepare the credentials used during registration and the service role used to manage the nodes after registration.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Rolling Back Configuration References by a Stable Name
prompt: A Parameter Store parameter has multiple versions. The application must continue referring to one approved version, and the operator does not want to change the code or parameter name for each release and rollback. Which operating method should be used?

choices.text: Attach a label to the approved version, and have the application reference the name together with the label.
choices.explanation: The application does not need to be modified, and the same label can be moved to another version.

choices.text: Have the application refer only to the latest version of the parameter.
choices.explanation: It could read an unapproved value as soon as that value is created.

choices.text: Add a fixed version number to the application code for every call.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid changing the application when the version changes.

choices.text: Attach an approved tag to the parameter and specify the same tag as the version number in GetParameter.
choices.explanation: Tags are not resolved as version selectors.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A parameter label can be attached to a specific version and moved to another version.
learning.concept: Keep the application’s label reference unchanged and control which version the label points to when adopting a release.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Aggregating Multi-Step Diagnostic Values in a Runbook
prompt: You need to obtain multiple responses in SSM Automation and produce one result using Python formatting and custom evaluation. The code must run in the Automation step runtime without sending commands to managed hosts. Which action should you use?

choices.text: Specify a Python runtime, handler, and inputs for aws:executeScript.
choices.explanation: This runs the aggregation logic without launching a command on a target host.

choices.text: Pass Python to aws:waitForAwsResourceProperty as the wait condition.
choices.explanation: This action polls a property; it does not provide a runtime for custom response processing.

choices.text: Specify Python to format multiple responses as one under aws:executeAwsApi as an API name.
choices.explanation: This action calls a specified AWS API operation; it does not execute arbitrary code.

choices.text: Run Python locally with aws:runCommand without specifying targets.
choices.explanation: Run Command requires managed nodes on which to execute the command.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: aws:executeScript runs a handler in a supported runtime as an Automation action.
learning.concept: Distinguish a single AWS API call or a command on a host from processing performed inside a runbook.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Replay Events from the Affected Period After Fixing the Rule
prompt: An archive was created in advance for an EventBridge custom event bus. During a certain time window, the target rule failed to capture events. After fixing the rule, you want to reprocess the events from that time window using the target rule on the original bus. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Start an archive replay and specify the time window and the rule to use for reprocessing.
choices.explanation: The saved events can be delivered to the corrected target rule on the same bus.

choices.text: Only disable the archive going forward and assume that the saved events will be sent automatically.
choices.explanation: A replay must be started to resend the events.

choices.text: Create a new rule DLQ and assume that all events that previously failed to match will be delivered to it.
choices.explanation: Previously unmatched events are not registered in a new DLQ.

choices.text: Rewrite the date with an input transformer and assume that the events will be retrieved again.
choices.explanation: An input transformer only formats input for new deliveries; it does not retrieve past events.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An archive replay returns recorded events to the original event bus within a specified time range.
learning.concept: Records for which delivery attempts failed differ from events that did not match a rule and are reprocessed from a saved archive.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Filter Events Before the Workflow
prompt: All SQS order events can be received by EventBridge Pipes. Events that are not in scope must not trigger an external API lookup; only the relevant events should be enriched by Lambda and passed to Step Functions. Where should the filtering be performed?

choices.text: Classify the events in Step Functions after the enrichment Lambda has completed the external lookup for every event.
choices.explanation: This performs unnecessary lookups and does not meet the requirement to exclude events first.

choices.text: Select order events by using the SQS visibility timeout.
choices.explanation: This setting controls when received messages become visible again; it cannot filter messages by their contents.

choices.text: Use the pipe's source event filter to match only the required order events.
choices.explanation: Events outside the scope can be excluded before the enrichment Lambda runs.

choices.text: Poll the source queue without conditions and reduce the target retry count.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce the number of events passed to the initial enrichment.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: In Pipes, filtering can be applied after reading from the source and before enrichment.
learning.concept: If there is no requirement to reprocess out-of-scope messages in SQS, the initial filter avoids unnecessary downstream calls.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Place One Persistent Task on Each EC2 Host
prompt: In an ECS cluster that uses EC2, you want to place one host log-forwarding task on each eligible EC2 container instance. The number of hosts changes, and you do not want to update the desired task count each time. The candidates can be selected with a placement constraint. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Start the task manually only once, regardless of detecting new hosts.
choices.explanation: Placement on hosts added later is not maintained.

choices.text: Start one log-forwarding service on Fargate and place it on each EC2 host.
choices.explanation: A Fargate task is not a method for keeping a task resident on selected EC2 container instances.

choices.text: Use REPLICA and set a fixed desired count equal to the current number of hosts.
choices.explanation: The desired count must be updated when the number of hosts changes, so one task per host cannot be maintained.

choices.text: Set the ECS service scheduling strategy to DAEMON and specify the required hosts with a placement constraint.
choices.explanation: Persistent tasks are placed as eligible EC2 hosts are added or removed.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The DAEMON scheduling strategy places one task on each active container instance that meets the constraint.
learning.concept: REPLICA manages the desired count for the service as a whole, which differs from maintaining one resident task per host.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Manage New and Old Task Sets with External Control
prompt: An internal external controller manages deployment of the corresponding ECS service. The controller must create task sets with separate task definitions and explicitly manage their steps. The service does not need to use the default ECS rolling update. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Keep the deployment controller as ECS and use only service updates to give the external controller complete control over the start order.
choices.explanation: The ECS controller advances a standard rolling update.

choices.text: Set the deployment controller for the corresponding service to EXTERNAL and operate the task sets from the controller.
choices.explanation: The new and old task sets for the service can be managed externally.

choices.text: Change REPLICA to DAEMON to make the deployment method external.
choices.explanation: The task placement strategy does not configure the controller for a new and old deployment.

choices.text: Only add a tag containing the external controller name to the task definition.
choices.explanation: A tag does not change the service's deployment method.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: With an external ECS deployment controller, an external system can manage operations on the task sets.
learning.concept: Distinguish service behavior that advances updates automatically from a method in which task sets are operated externally.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Declare Placement on Dedicated Nodes
prompt: Some EKS nodes are reserved for dedicated batch workloads. You need to prevent general Pods from using them and place batch Pods only in that node group. The administrator can manage the required Pod settings. Which combination should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Configure only a toleration on the batch Pods and allow them to be scheduled on all nodes.
choices.explanation: This does not restrict placement to the dedicated nodes.

choices.text: Specify the toleration corresponding to the batch Pods and a nodeSelector for the dedicated label.
choices.explanation: This tolerates the taint and selects the dedicated nodes.

choices.text: Add the dedicated-node toleration to general Pods to avoid placing them there.
choices.explanation: Because the toleration permits the taint, it does not avoid placement on those nodes.

choices.text: Set a label and a NoSchedule taint on the dedicated node group.
choices.explanation: This identifies the target nodes while preventing general Pods from using them.

choices.text: Increase the number of dedicated nodes and let the scheduler decide without using labels or taints.
choices.explanation: There is no rule that separates placement for general and batch workloads.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A taint and toleration control whether placement is permitted, while a label and nodeSelector select the target nodes.
learning.concept: A toleration alone does not prevent scheduling on other compatible nodes.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Replicate Only the Images to Be Deployed Across Regions
prompt: You deploy ECS services to multiple Regions in the same account. You want only images in repositories under the release/ prefix that will be pushed in the future to be automatically replicated to another Region, while repositories with experimental names should not be replicated. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Configure the destination Region and a release/ repository filter in the source registry.
choices.explanation: This replicates images pushed in the future to matching repositories to another Region.

choices.text: Include release/ in the image tags and enable replication for all registries.
choices.explanation: Replication filters specify a repository-name prefix, not an image tag.

choices.text: Set release/ in a lifecycle policy to filter only the images subject to deletion.
choices.explanation: A lifecycle policy controls retention and deletion; it does not configure image transfer.

choices.text: Create a pull-through cache only in the destination and require it to synchronize to the destination whenever an image is pushed.
choices.explanation: Fetching through a cache and replicating an image after it is pushed are separate functions.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: ECR cross-Region replication rules can filter repositories by repository-name prefix.
learning.concept: Distinguish the condition for selecting repositories from the setting that controls retention of existing images.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Keep the Instance from a Failed Build for Analysis
prompt: When creating a new OS image with EC2 Image Builder, a custom build step fails. The failure cannot be determined from CloudWatch logs, so you need to inspect the failed build instance during the next validation run and have the responsible operator clean it up afterward. What should you change?

choices.text: Set terminateInstanceOnFailure to false in the validation infrastructure configuration.
choices.explanation: This keeps the instance for the applicable failure so you can inspect the evidence.

choices.text: Change only the startup IMDS settings of the AMI used by Image Builder.
choices.explanation: These settings control metadata access and do not affect automatic termination after a failure.

choices.text: Add the Region in which to share the AMI to the distribution settings.
choices.explanation: This does not change the instance-termination flow after a build failure.

choices.text: Extend the lifecycle retention period for old AMIs.
choices.explanation: This retains stored artifacts; it does not retain the build instance.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The infrastructure configuration setting terminateInstanceOnFailure controls whether an instance launched for a build or test is terminated after a failure.
learning.concept: Log destinations and image-retention rules do not configure the failed instance to remain after reporting.

category: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
examDomain: デプロイ・プロビジョニングと自動化
title: Apply Changes to the Pipeline's Own Definition
prompt: You added a new deployment stage to an existing AWS CDK Pipelines pipeline definition. Source retrieval and synthesis succeed, but self-mutation is disabled, so the new stage is not created in the next pipeline execution. How should you enable continuous application of the change?

choices.text: Only delete the CDK context cache.
choices.explanation: Referenced values might be retrieved again, but the definition is not applied while self-mutation remains disabled.

choices.text: Deploy a change that enables self-mutation to the pipeline stack once, and then have subsequent changes reflected by SelfMutate.
choices.explanation: The pipeline can then apply later definition changes to itself.

choices.text: Change the application bucket lifecycle after synthesis.
choices.explanation: This manages a deployment resource; it does not change the pipeline structure.

choices.text: Rerun only the application's deployment stage.
choices.explanation: This does not apply changes to the stack that defines the pipeline.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: CDK Pipelines self-mutation applies changes in the synthesized pipeline definition to the pipeline itself.
learning.concept: The process for deploying service resources differs from the process for updating the pipeline structure.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Setting an upper bound on external principals’ permissions for organizational resources
prompt: You want to prevent unexpected access to an S3 bucket in an AWS Organizations member account by IAM principals belonging to accounts outside the organization. Each team manages its own bucket policy. Which organizational feature can impose an upper bound on the permissions that such principals have on member buckets?

choices.text: Apply an RCP with S3 external-access conditions to the target OU.
choices.explanation: This applies an organizational limit to the target resources even when an external principal is allowed by a resource policy.

choices.text: Use only an SCP on the target OU to directly restrict principals outside the organization.
choices.explanation: An SCP constrains principals in the target member accounts; it does not apply to external principals.

choices.text: Use an organization tag policy to list the permitted account IDs as tag values.
choices.explanation: Standardizing available tag values does not create a permissions boundary for external access.

choices.text: Configure external-access conditions in the backup policy for member accounts.
choices.explanation: A backup policy does not impose an upper bound on access-permission evaluation.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An RCP defines an upper bound on applicable permissions for supported resources in target member accounts.
learning.concept: An SCP, which sets limits on principals in member accounts, constrains a different target.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Comparing results for policies with context
prompt: A policy applied to an IAM role allows an existing operation only when the team value in PrincipalTag matches a specified value. Before applying the change, test the evaluation when the tag matches and when it does not, without performing the production operation. What should you do?

choices.text: In the IAM policy simulator, specify the action and resource, then compare the evaluations while switching the context for the corresponding tag.
choices.explanation: You can compare Allow and Deny under the tested conditions without operating on a real resource.

choices.text: If Access Analyzer’s policy syntax validation produces no warnings, conclude that the execution result is the same for every tag value.
choices.explanation: This validates policy syntax and design; it does not evaluate a specific request context.

choices.text: Read successful CloudTrail logs from before the change and conclude that the tag condition will also succeed after the update.
choices.explanation: Past successful requests do not establish that the proposed condition will be allowed.

choices.text: Download the credentials report and look for evaluation results for each tag value.
choices.explanation: The credentials report describes user-credential status; it does not simulate condition evaluation.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The IAM policy simulator can evaluate a policy by supplying the target action, resource, and required context values.
learning.concept: Align the context supplied in the simulation with the context created by the actual call.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Tracking recent management operations in the relevant Region
prompt: You need to determine who changed the instance type of a development EC2 instance in one Region three weeks ago. You did not create a trail or CloudTrail Lake in advance. Before configuring additional collection, what should you inspect in the history retained by default?

choices.text: Create an S3 trail that emits only data events after the investigation.
choices.explanation: The past EC2 management event in question is not covered by that configuration.

choices.text: Query the configuration of the EC2 CloudWatch agent.
choices.explanation: OS-level metric-collection settings cannot identify the principal that called an AWS management API.

choices.text: Check only the instance tags to identify who performed the change.
choices.explanation: The current tags do not identify the caller of a past management API request.

choices.text: Search management events in CloudTrail event history for the Region where the EC2 instance was operated.
choices.explanation: Even without a trail, you can review management API activity from the relevant period.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: CloudTrail Event history provides the last 90 days of management events for each Region by default.
learning.concept: Data events and longer-term retention require advance planning, such as configuring trails.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Obtaining security feedback during design before implementation
prompt: AWS Security Agent is available. The team wants to review a design document for a new service against its internal security requirements before implementation. It needs findings on the design document, while evaluating the configuration of the running service will be done later. Which feature should be used?

choices.text: Scan vulnerabilities in packages on running EC2 instances with Inspector.
choices.explanation: This does not compare a design document with the team’s requirements.

choices.text: Use AWS Config only to check the compliance status of existing resources.
choices.explanation: It does not directly review an unimplemented design document.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail management events and generate findings from the design document.
choices.explanation: This configures API recording; it does not generate findings from a design document.

choices.text: Enable the organization’s security requirements and submit the design document for an AWS Security Agent design review.
choices.explanation: This compares design-stage decisions with the specified requirements.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A design review uses the specified design material to identify inconsistencies with the applicable requirements.
learning.concept: A design-stage review and detection from already deployed resources use different evaluation inputs.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Applying an Operations Standard to Multiple Accounts Through an OU
prompt: You operate Security Hub CSPM in AWS Organizations. You want to enable the same standards together in the home Region and linked Regions, including for new accounts in a specified OU. Other OUs must be allowed to follow different operating policies. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Enable the standards only in the delegated administrator account and leave the remaining accounts unchanged.
choices.explanation: Local settings in the delegated administrator account alone cannot be applied to the target OU.

choices.text: Write the API that enables the standards as an Allow statement in an SCP and attach it to the OU.
choices.explanation: Allowing the API in an SCP does not mean that the API was executed in each account.

choices.text: Aggregate findings in the home Region and assume that the enabled standards are automatically synchronized for each account.
choices.explanation: Aggregation alone does not change the standards configured for each account.

choices.text: Have the delegated administrator use central configuration and associate a configuration policy with the required standards enabled to the target OU.
choices.explanation: This applies a common configuration to the accounts in the target OU across the home Region and linked Regions.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: With Security Hub CSPM central configuration, the delegated administrator associates configuration policies with accounts or OUs.
learning.concept: Aggregation and configuration application are separate functions. Associating a policy with an OU causes the configuration to be inherited by accounts in that OU.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Receiving Contact from the Service During an Attack with Service Disruption
prompt: You have an ALB protected by Shield Advanced. If an attack affecting the ALB also affects application availability, you want the Shield Response Team to contact the responsible person before your organization opens a case. The required support conditions are met. Which two preparations should you make?

choices.text: Configure only a health check for the ALB target group and do not associate a health check with Shield.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the Route 53 health check association that the SRT uses.

choices.text: Associate a Route 53 health check representing application availability with the protected resource in Shield Advanced.
choices.explanation: The health check provides information that can be used to assess availability when an attack is detected.

choices.text: Specify a WAF log destination instead of the SRT contact information.
choices.explanation: A log destination does not provide the information required to contact the responsible person.

choices.text: Switch to Shield Standard only and enable the same contact feature.
choices.explanation: The specified proactive engagement feature is provided by Shield Advanced.

choices.text: Enable proactive engagement and register valid contact information that the SRT can use.
choices.explanation: When the conditions are met, the SRT can use this information to contact the responsible person.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Shield Advanced proactive engagement uses a health check associated with the protected resource and registered contact information.
learning.concept: Prepare a check that represents the application's actual state and contact information for someone who can respond to the incident.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Managing a Common Set of Destinations Across Multiple Controls
prompt: Across multiple VPCs, the same team manages a set of destination CIDRs permitted for traffic leaving to an internal network. You want each security group's outbound destinations to reference the same named set and do not want to edit individual groups when a CIDR changes. What should you use?

choices.text: Specify the name of a private DNS hosted zone in the outbound rule as the destination.
choices.explanation: A regular security group outbound destination cannot be an arbitrary DNS hosted zone name.

choices.text: Duplicate a rule in each security group for every destination CIDR.
choices.explanation: A destination change would require the same update in every group.

choices.text: Register the CIDRs only in the route tables and allow outbound traffic to any destination in the security groups.
choices.explanation: Having a route is different from restricting permitted destinations in a security group.

choices.text: Put the destination CIDRs in a customer-managed prefix list and reference it from the applicable outbound rules.
choices.explanation: You can maintain the set of destinations used by the referencing rules by updating the common list.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A customer-managed prefix list can be referenced from security group rules.
learning.concept: This separates management of the CIDR set from the rules that determine which traffic is allowed.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Granting AWS Permissions Used by Pods per Service Account
prompt: Pod Identity is available in Amazon EKS. Only batch Pods need to read a specific S3 prefix. The node role has no permissions for the target S3 resources, and a Kubernetes service account dedicated to the batch workload has already been created. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Add the batch workload's S3 permissions to the node's instance profile.
choices.explanation: The permissions would not be restricted to the target service account.

choices.text: Add s3 to the allowed API groups in the Kubernetes Role.
choices.explanation: Kubernetes API RBAC settings do not grant access permissions to AWS S3.

choices.text: Provide the corresponding Pod Identity Agent and associate a least-privilege IAM role with the target namespace and service account.
choices.explanation: This avoids granting the permissions to other service accounts on the same node.

choices.text: Configure the batch workload's role on the default service account in every namespace.
choices.explanation: Workloads outside the target scope could run with the same permissions.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An EKS Pod Identity association assigns an IAM role to a namespace and service account in the cluster.
learning.concept: You can configure the credentials received by the application at the workload level without changing the node IAM role.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Updating an externally issued certificate while preserving the same association
prompt: An ALB uses an externally issued TLS certificate imported into ACM. A new certificate chain and corresponding private key have been received from the issuer. What should be done to update the certificate while keeping the ALB certificate association pointing to the same reference?

choices.text: Import the new certificate under a different ARN and leave the ALB reference unchanged.
choices.explanation: The certificate under the existing ARN is not updated.

choices.text: Add one DNS validation record and wait for ACM-managed renewal of the externally issued certificate.
choices.explanation: Imported externally issued certificates are not automatically renewed this way.

choices.text: Import only the root certificate under a different ARN and wait until the current certificate expires.
choices.explanation: The new contents are not applied to the associated server certificate.

choices.text: Specify the existing certificate ARN and re-import the new certificate, chain, and key.
choices.explanation: The ARN is preserved, so the existing association is retained.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A certificate imported into ACM can be re-imported using its existing ARN.
learning.concept: Managed renewal of an ACM-issued certificate differs from re-importing an externally issued certificate.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Designing credential switching during rotation
prompt: Use the rotation template for the corresponding RDS engine and Secrets Manager. An application frequently opens new connections, and the design should avoid changing the password of a single database user first during rotation. Two users with the same permissions can be managed. What should be selected?

choices.text: Prepare a management secret and configure rotation using the alternating-users strategy.
choices.explanation: The user to be used next can be updated separately from the current user.

choices.text: Use the single-user strategy and assume that the database password change and the application's retrieval always complete at exactly the same time.
choices.explanation: This cannot avoid access to the previous value between the two stages.

choices.text: Simply duplicate the same user and value in two secrets.
choices.explanation: A database does not maintain two passwords for that same user in this configuration.

choices.text: Use automatic KMS key rotation to alternate the database credential users.
choices.explanation: Updating KMS key material does not change database users or passwords.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The alternating-users strategy updates the inactive user and then switches the connection secret to that user.
learning.concept: Consider the period during which the previous user's ability to connect and the timing of secret retrieval can be out of sync.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Passing a noncompliant resource ID to remediation
prompt: An AWS Config rule detects a test resource that became noncompliant after a change. An approved SSM runbook accepts a resource ID as input and changes only the detected resource. What should be configured to remediate violations automatically without hard-coding an individual ID?

choices.text: Enter one fixed value for the runbook's resource ID and reuse it for every violation.
choices.explanation: Because the same resource is remediated every time, the actual violating resource might not be processed.

choices.text: Only add more notification destinations to the Config rule.
choices.explanation: Additional destinations do not associate the SSM operation with the violating resource.

choices.text: Associate automatic remediation with the Config rule and pass Resource ID to the corresponding runbook parameter.
choices.explanation: The runbook can use the detected resource as its target.

choices.text: Only view the findings in an aggregator account.
choices.explanation: Aggregation provides visibility but does not execute remediation.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: AWS Config remediation settings can pass the violating resource's ID to a runbook parameter.
learning.concept: Remediation requires configuring both an approved action and its association with the target resource in addition to evaluation.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Removing one Region from service while preserving connections
prompt: A standard Global Accelerator has endpoint groups in two Regions. During maintenance, new traffic to one Region must stop. The other Region is healthy, and the client-facing destination IP must not change. Which setting should be used?

choices.text: Swap the accelerator's listener ports.
choices.explanation: This does not remove only a specific Region from service.

choices.text: Create another accelerator and distribute its IP address to all users.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to control traffic while preserving the destination.

choices.text: Set the traffic dial for the endpoint group in the maintenance Region to 0.
choices.explanation: The client-facing destination remains unchanged, and new traffic can be sent to the other healthy group. Existing connections are not terminated by changing the dial.

choices.text: Set the weight of only one endpoint in one Region to 0.
choices.explanation: Traffic can still be distributed to other endpoints in the same group.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The traffic dial controls the percentage of traffic sent to an endpoint group at the Region level.
learning.concept: Endpoint weights control distribution among endpoints within the same group.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Resolving a Private Hosted Zone from On-Premises DNS
prompt: Connectivity from the on-premises network to the VPC through Direct Connect or a VPN has already been confirmed. The on-premises DNS server should query AWS only for the Route 53 private hosted zone associated with the VPC, while resolving all other names as it does today. Which configuration meets these requirements? Select two.

choices.text: Forward queries directly to the VPC's reserved Resolver addresses without creating an inbound endpoint.
choices.explanation: An endpoint is required for DNS queries originating from an external network.

choices.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in a VPC that can resolve the zone, and allow TCP and UDP DNS queries from the on-premises DNS server.
choices.explanation: The inbound endpoint provides a Resolver connection point in a VPC reachable from on premises.

choices.text: Move the zone to a public hosted zone with the same name and resolve it over the internet.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to keep private information private and forward only the target zone internally.

choices.text: Use an outbound endpoint as the destination for queries entering from on premises.
choices.explanation: An outbound endpoint is used to send queries from the VPC to external destinations; it does not receive queries from outside.

choices.text: Configure the on-premises DNS server to conditionally forward the target private hosted zone to the endpoint's IP addresses.
choices.explanation: This leaves the existing resolution path for all other names unchanged.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: An inbound endpoint can be used for queries from an on-premises DNS server to the VPC Resolver.
learning.concept: Provide an endpoint that receives the traffic, and forward only the target zone from the on-premises DNS server.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Returning Multiple Healthy Destinations in DNS
prompt: Clients can retry connections to multiple returned IPv4 addresses. When healthy destinations are available, you want Route 53 to return up to eight addresses that individually pass health checks for a public name, allowing the client to choose among them. Which DNS routing policy is appropriate?

choices.text: Register each address as a multivalue answer record with a health check.
choices.explanation: Each value can be evaluated independently, and one response can include multiple healthy values.

choices.text: Put all addresses in one simple record and use individual health checks to exclude only the affected values.
choices.explanation: Simple routing does not apply health checks to individual values in that manner.

choices.text: Configure primary and secondary failover records.
choices.explanation: This does not continuously return multiple healthy values together.

choices.text: Configure all addresses as latency records in the same Region.
choices.explanation: Latency-based routing selects a low-latency destination for the user; it does not meet the requirement to return multiple individually healthy values.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Multivalue answer routing can include multiple healthy records in a single DNS response.
learning.concept: Returning destinations at the DNS layer is different from a load balancer receiving connections and distributing requests.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Adding the Same CORS Header to Cached Responses
prompt: CloudFront serves static fonts to designated websites. Without changing the origin or the file contents, you need each behavior to add a consistent Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, including on cache hits. What should you configure?

choices.text: Add the allowed origins as a TXT record in Route 53.
choices.explanation: This does not change the CORS header in the HTTP response returned to the browser.

choices.text: Associate a response headers policy that specifies the allowed origins with the target behavior.
choices.explanation: The specified CORS headers can be applied even to responses served from the cache.

choices.text: Increase the TTL in the cache policy and configure nothing to add the CORS header.
choices.explanation: Changing the retention period does not generate the header.

choices.text: Configure Access-Control-Allow-Origin only in an origin request policy.
choices.explanation: An origin request policy controls requests sent to the origin; it does not add a response header for viewers.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A response headers policy adds or modifies headers in responses returned by a behavior to viewers.
learning.concept: Its role differs from the cache key and from request headers sent to the origin.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Collecting VPN Negotiation Logs
prompt: IKE establishment intermittently fails on one tunnel of a Site-to-Site VPN. The AWS-side tunnel state and traffic volume were insufficient to narrow down the cause. For the next attempt, you want to inspect the IKE progress and errors on the AWS side in chronological order. What should you configure?

choices.text: Collect only the CloudTrail records for configuration changes to the VPN connection.
choices.explanation: AWS API activity records are different from IKE negotiation during connection establishment.

choices.text: Assume that the VPC Flow Logs for the destination subnets include the IKE authentication result.
choices.explanation: VPC flow information does not record the state of IKE inside the VPN tunnel.

choices.text: Enable Site-to-Site VPN logs for the target tunnel and send them to CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: This provides details about IKE negotiation that are not available from metrics alone.

choices.text: Add graphs for TunnelDataIn and TunnelDataOut for each tunnel.
choices.explanation: These metrics show traffic volume but do not record the reason for an IKE failure.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Site-to-Site VPN tunnel logs record information such as IKE negotiation details.
learning.concept: Use metrics to determine whether a tunnel is up and logs to examine the negotiation process.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Checking VPN session connection times
prompt: A company wants to track in the future whether a connection attempt to its AWS Client VPN succeeded at a particular time and which sessions disconnected and when. Recording individual packets forwarded through the VPN is not the primary objective. What should be enabled?

choices.text: Add query logging to the DNS resolver used by the destination.
choices.explanation: Name-resolution records cannot confirm VPN connection attempts and disconnections.

choices.text: Update the authentication rules and assume that records for all connections will remain in CloudTrail management events.
choices.explanation: Management API records are different from client-session logs.

choices.text: Enable connection logging for the target Client VPN endpoint and configure a CloudWatch Logs destination.
choices.explanation: This makes connection information about the sessions available for investigation.

choices.text: Enable only VPC Flow Logs for the related subnets.
choices.explanation: Network flows can be recorded, but the start and end of logical VPN sessions are not captured as dedicated VPN logs.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Sending Client VPN connection logs to CloudWatch Logs records connection attempts and the start and end of connections.
learning.concept: Distinguish between recording network flows and recording the sessions recognized by the VPN.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Investigating when a connection closes during inactivity
prompt: A WebSocket connection through an ALB closes when neither the client nor the target sends data for approximately 60 seconds or more. The application timeout is longer, and only the load balancer's inactivity period needs to be adjusted. Which attribute should be changed?

choices.text: Increase only client_keep_alive.seconds.
choices.explanation: This controls the maximum duration of an HTTP connection; it does not change the inactivity condition.

choices.text: Check the ALB's idle_timeout.timeout_seconds and adjust it to the required inactivity period.
choices.explanation: This changes the condition under which the ALB closes a connection when no data is being transferred.

choices.text: Reduce the health check interval to less than 60 seconds.
choices.explanation: Separate health-check traffic does not reset the inactivity period of a viewer's WebSocket connection.

choices.text: Increase only the target's deregistration_delay.
choices.explanation: This setting applies to existing processing when a target is deregistered.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The ALB connection idle timeout manages the period during which no data is sent or received.
learning.concept: Its trigger condition differs from the HTTP client keep-alive setting and the target deregistration delay.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Connecting to a private service in another Region
prompt: A network service is provided in a VPC in supported Region A. The consumer VPC is in supported Region B, and no public connectivity or VPC-to-VPC network connection should be added. How can the provider select the consumer Region and principal and allow a private connection?

choices.text: Create an S3 gateway endpoint in Region B and select the service provider's NLB.
choices.explanation: A gateway endpoint does not create an interface connection to this custom service.

choices.text: Register only the service name in the consumer VPC's private DNS and create no connection resource.
choices.explanation: DNS alone does not add a PrivateLink path between the VPCs.

choices.text: On the provider side, allow Region B and the consumer principal; on the consumer side, configure an interface endpoint that specifies the service in Region A.
choices.explanation: The consumer can connect privately to the service specified by the interface endpoint.

choices.text: Configure inter-Region VPC peering and bidirectional routes.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to expose the service by service and avoid a network connection between the VPCs.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A supported PrivateLink endpoint service can allow access across Regions.
learning.concept: Align the provider's supported Region and principal permissions with the service Region specified by the consumer's endpoint.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Connecting IPv6 clients to an IPv4-only service
prompt: An EC2 instance in an IPv6-only subnet must connect to an external IPv4-only API that has a DNS name. A public NAT gateway with existing IPv4 reachability is available, and no IPv4 support will be added to the application. Which two VPC configurations should be combined?

choices.text: Assume that DNS64 alone provides access to the IPv4 network and add no route.
choices.explanation: Name resolution does not translate packets to IPv4.

choices.text: Add only an IPv4 0.0.0.0/0 route for the IPv6-only source.
choices.explanation: An IPv4 route does not apply to packets with a synthesized IPv6 destination.

choices.text: Route 64:ff9b::/96 to the existing NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: This sends traffic for synthesized destinations to the NAT64 translation path.

choices.text: Route 64:ff9b::/96 to an egress-only internet gateway.
choices.explanation: That gateway handles outbound IPv6 traffic but does not translate it to IPv4.

choices.text: Enable DNS64 for the subnet and use the VPC Resolver on the target clients.
choices.explanation: When only an A record exists, this can synthesize a corresponding IPv6 destination.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Route 53 Resolver DNS64 returns a synthesized IPv6 address for the IPv4 destination, and the NAT gateway performs NAT64 translation to IPv4.
learning.concept: Provide both destination name resolution and a packet path that translates traffic for the synthesized destination.

category: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
examDomain: ネットワークとコンテンツ配信
title: Keep an approved IPv4 address after replacing an instance
prompt: A partner adds the public IPv4 address of a single-instance EC2 service to an allow list. After an instance failure in an Availability Zone, the partner wants to manually switch to a standby instance while continuing to use the same IPv4 address without being asked to change the allow list. What should be prepared?

choices.text: Record the automatically assigned public IPv4 address and request the same address for the standby instance.
choices.explanation: An automatically assigned public IPv4 address cannot be reserved and reassigned in this way.

choices.text: Shorten the DNS TTL and treat the IPv4 address registered in the allow list as unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the value during a DNS switch does not preserve the original IPv4 address in the allow list.

choices.text: Give the standby instance the same security group name as the production instance.
choices.explanation: Allow rules for source access and assignment of the public IPv4 address used for external connections are separate concerns.

choices.text: Allocate an Elastic IP address to the account, use it for the service, and reassociate it with the standby instance during the switch.
choices.explanation: The same public IPv4 address can be assigned to the connection target after the replacement.

title: Keep both directions of traffic on the same inspection node
prompt: An inspection VPC in multiple Availability Zones is connected to a Transit Gateway. Stateful appliances are used, and although the route passes through the inspection VPC, the forward and return paths of the same flow may be sent to appliances in different Availability Zones. Which attribute should be configured to keep the flow on the inspection path in the same Availability Zone?

choices.text: Disable route propagation for the attachments in all spoke VPCs.
choices.explanation: Stopping route propagation does not configure Availability Zone symmetry for inspection traffic.

choices.text: Enable appliance mode only on the attachment of one spoke VPC.
choices.explanation: Because the stateful appliances are in the inspection VPC, the target attachment is different.

choices.text: Enable appliance mode on the Transit Gateway attachment for the inspection VPC.
choices.explanation: This allows the same Availability Zone of the inspection VPC to be used for the forward and return paths of the same flow.

choices.text: Only increase the allowed ports in the network ACL of the source VPC.
choices.explanation: Allowing the connection does not align the forward and return paths through the inspection appliance.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Transit Gateway appliance mode uses the same Availability Zone path in the inspection VPC for the duration of a flow.
learning.concept: Even when routes to the inspection VPC are correct, stateful appliances require symmetric paths in both directions.

title: Reserve a network range before assigning it
prompt: IPAM is used to manage a Regional pool. A specific CIDR must be reserved for a VPC whose creation date has not been decided, and other teams must not use the same pool for that CIDR before that date. What can be used to reserve only the CIDR without creating an empty VPC first?

choices.text: Disable the IPAM discovery scope until the creation date.
choices.explanation: This does not reserve the range so that other teams cannot acquire it.

choices.text: Register the same range as a Route 53 Resolver forwarding destination.
choices.explanation: Managing DNS query destinations does not constrain address allocation from the pool.

choices.text: Allocate a manually selected CIDR from the Regional pool and record the future use in the description.
choices.explanation: IPAM can manage the range as allocated even before the VPC is created.

choices.text: Only describe the range in a tag policy without allocating it.
choices.explanation: The range remains unallocated in IPAM and could be used for another allocation.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: IPAM manual allocation can reserve a CIDR from a pool without immediately creating a resource.
learning.concept: An allocation registered as a reservation is different from duplicate detection performed by monitoring.
